Audiologist & Hearing Aids in Alexandria
Roberts Hearing Clinic

Roberts Hearing Clinic provides expert hearing care to help you stay connected to the sounds that matter most. From comprehensive hearing evaluations to advanced hearing aid solutions, our audiologist is here to support your hearing health with personalized care. Schedule an appointment today and take the first step toward better hearing!

We offer a full range of hearing services to help you hear clearly and comfortably. Our specialists provide comprehensive hearing assessments to diagnose hearing loss and recommend personalized solutions. Whether you need a hearing test, tinnitus care, or expert guidance on hearing aids, we’re here to support your hearing health every step of the way.
Audiology Services In Alexandria, LA
Hearing Evaluations
Your journey to better hearing begins with a thorough assessment. Our specialists use state-of-the-art testing to identify hearing loss and create customized solutions that fit your lifestyle.
Tinnitus Support

If you experience ringing or buzzing in your ears, our tinnitus support can help determine the cause. We offer effective options, including sound therapy and management strategies, to provide long-term relief.
Diagnostic Services
We provide in-depth diagnostic testing to evaluate hearing health and detect any underlying conditions. Our team ensures precise results and guides you toward the best treatment options.
Hearing Aid Services

From choosing the right hearing aid to ongoing maintenance, we provide expert support every step of the way. Our services include fittings, adjustments, cleanings, and repairs to keep your hearing aids working at their best.
Hearing Aid Fittings
A well-fitted hearing aid ensures comfort and optimal sound quality. We customize your device for a seamless and natural listening experience, tailored to your specific hearing needs.
Hearing Aid Repair
If your hearing aid isn’t functioning properly, our team provides fast and effective repairs. Whether it’s a simple adjustment or a more complex issue, we’re here to help.
Hearing Aids & Hearing Protection In Alexandria, LA
Hearing Aids
We offer a wide range of advanced, discreet hearing aids to match your lifestyle. Our team will help you find the perfect fit for clear and natural sound.
Custom Ear Protection
Safeguard your hearing with custom earplugs and earmolds, designed for comfort and protection against noise, water, and other environmental factors.
Hearing Aid Batteries and Accessories
Ensure your hearing aids stay powered and perform at their best with our selection of high-quality batteries and accessories.

Frequently Asked Questions
Can’t find the answers you’re looking for? Contact Us.
Can you self-refer to an audiologist or hearing aid specialists?

Yes, you can book an appointment with an audiologist or hearing aid specialists without needing a referral from a doctor or nurse. This is called self-referral and allows you to seek hearing care directly. However, many insurance plans and Medicare may require one for coverage.
How is hearing loss diagnosed?

Hearing loss is identified through a detailed hearing evaluation performed by an audiologist or hearing specialist. This assessment includes various tests to measure hearing ability and detect any underlying issues. After the evaluation, the audiologist will explain your results, determine the type and severity of hearing loss, and recommend appropriate solutions such as hearing aids, medical treatment, or other hearing care options.
What type of hearing aid do I need?

The best hearing aid for you depends on your level of hearing loss, lifestyle, and personal preferences. Hearing aids come in various styles, each designed to offer different benefits. An audiologist can assess your needs and help you choose the most suitable option based on your hearing ability, dexterity, daily activities, and cosmetic considerations.
How do I know if I have hearing loss?
Hearing loss often develops gradually, making it hard to recognize at first. Some common signs include:
Frequently asking others to repeat themselves
Difficulty following conversations in noisy settings
Increasing the volume on the TV or phone higher than others prefer
Feeling like people are mumbling or not speaking clearly
Trouble hearing high-pitched voices, such as children or women
Experiencing ringing or buzzing in the ears (tinnitus)
Feeling mentally drained from trying to listen and keep up with conversations

If you notice any of these signs, a hearing evaluation with an audiologist can help determine whether you have hearing loss and what steps to take. Early detection and treatment can improve your overall well-being and communication.

About Roberts Hearing Clinic
Roberts Hearing Clinic is an audiology and hearing aid clinic with expert audiologists providing hearing tests, tinnitus evaluations, and professional hearing services in Alexandria, LA.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we’re proud to serve the Alexandria, LA community with friendly, professional hearing care you can count on.
Our mission is simple: to help you hear your best so you can stay connected to the people and moments that matter most.

We understand that hearing loss can affect every part of your life-and we’re here to help you take the next step with confidence. Whether you need a hearing test, new hearing aids, or support with your current devices, our experienced team is ready to guide you with care and compassion.

Roberts Hearing Clinic offers a full range of hearing services, including comprehensive hearing evaluations, personalized hearing aid fittings, repairs, and follow-up care. We stay up to date with the latest hearing technology and work closely with you to find the best solution for your hearing needs and lifestyle.
We’re proud to be a part of the Alexandria community and are dedicated to providing honest, personalized care to every patient who walks through our doors.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, your hearing health is our top priority -because better hearing means a better life.

children.text: Home » Julie Tucker
Julie Tucker
Meet Julie Tucker — Hearing Instrument Specialist

Julie Tucker became part of the Roberts Hearing Clinic team in 2021, initially assisting the Audiologist. It wasn’t long before her curiosity was sparked by the work of the Audiologist, and she felt called to make a deeper impact.

Motivated by the sheer joy of helping patients hear—some for the very first time—and witnessing the emotional moments when they reconnect with loved ones, Julie pursued and earned her license as a Hearing Instrument Specialist.
Today, she arrives each morning with genuine excitement, ready to provide compassionate, professional care to those seeking better hearing and a better quality of life.

Outside the clinic, Julie embraces life’s adventures. Whether exploring new destinations or enjoying the comforts of home, she finds joy in cooking, diving into good books, and cherishing time with family and friends.
Roberts Hearing Clinic

Hearing Evaluations
Your journey to better hearing begins with a thorough assessment. Our specialists use state-of-the-art testing to identify hearing loss and create customized solutions that fit your lifestyle.
Tinnitus Support

If you experience ringing or buzzing in your ears, our tinnitus support can help determine the cause. We offer effective options, including sound therapy and management strategies, to provide long-term relief.
Diagnostic Services
We provide in-depth diagnostic testing to evaluate hearing health and detect any underlying conditions. Our team ensures precise results and guides you toward the best treatment options.
Hearing Aid Services

From choosing the right hearing aid to ongoing maintenance, we provide expert support every step of the way. Our services include fittings, adjustments, cleanings, and repairs to keep your hearing aids working at their best.
Hearing Aid Fittings
A well-fitted hearing aid ensures comfort and optimal sound quality. We customize your device for a seamless and natural listening experience, tailored to your specific hearing needs.
Hearing Aid Repair
If your hearing aid isn’t functioning properly, our team provides fast and effective repairs. Whether it’s a simple adjustment or a more complex issue, we’re here to help.

Katie Pierce, M.C.D.
Katie Pierce, M.C.D. is an audiologist providing hearing tests and hearing aids in Alexandria, LA

Katie Pierce, M.C.D., is a licensed Audiologist at Roberts Hearing Clinic. A Louisiana native, she grew up in the area and returned after earning her Master’s Degree from LSU Medical Center in New Orleans in 1992.
Katie enjoys the outdoors and can often be found playing darts or cornhole, spending time with her family and friends, and staying involved in her church community.

With experience caring for patients of all ages—from infants to older adults—Katie values the importance of early diagnosis and treatment. She is dedicated to providing high-quality hearing care with kindness, compassion, and a personal touch.

children.text: Home » Hearing » Best Way to Clean Ears: Tips From Audiologists in Alexandria, LA
Best Way to Clean Ears: Tips From Audiologists in Alexandria, LA
Julie Tucker
January 23, 2025
Hearing

When it comes to personal hygiene, many people assume that cleaning their ears should be part of their routine—especially when they see wax. But believe it or not, your ears are actually self-cleaning. That’s right! Most of the time, they don’t need your help. Still, knowing when and how to clean your ears safely can prevent discomfort, hearing issues, and even injury.
If you’ve ever asked yourself, “What’s the best way to clean my ears?” this article is for you.
Our expert audiologists in Alexandria, LA share their thoughts on the best way to clean your ears.
The Logic Behind Ear Wax
Ear wax, or cerumen, often gets a bad rap, but it actually plays an important role in keeping your ears healthy. Produced by glands in your ear canal, cerumen helps:
Trap dust and debris before it reaches your eardrum
Protect your ears from bacteria, fungi, and water
Keep your ear canal lubricated and prevent dryness or itching

In most cases, old wax naturally moves toward the outer ear and flakes away. However, many people interfere with this process by using cotton swabs, hairpins, or other sharp objects—a habit that can push wax deeper into the canal or even damage the eardrum.

Poking around in your ears can do more harm than good. Not only can it cause pain, but it can also increase your risk of infection, bleeding, or permanent hearing loss. The safest strategy? Learn to work with your body’s natural process, not against it.
If you feel like you really need to get your ears cleaned, it’s best to let a professional do it.
Best Way to Clean Ears: Should You Clean Your Ears at All?

In most cases, you don’t need to clean your ears manually. The skin inside your ear canal grows outward, helping wax and debris make their way out naturally. A simple wipe with a warm, damp cloth around the outer ear is usually enough.
However, there are times when earwax can build up and cause problems. This condition is known as cerumen impaction, and it happens when wax gets stuck and hardens inside the ear canal.
Signs of Cerumen Impaction:
A feeling of fullness in the ear
Earache or discomfort
Ringing in the ears (tinnitus)
Itchiness or discharge
Trouble hearing in one or both ears
Dizziness or imbalance
If you notice any of these symptoms, do not try to remove the wax yourself. It’s important to see a hearing care professional or doctor who can safely assess and treat the issue.
Ear Cleaning Do’s and Don’ts
Do:
Use a damp washcloth to clean the outer ear
Try over-the-counter ear drops to soften wax (if recommended)
Keep your ears dry, especially after bathing or swimming
Visit an audiologist if you suspect a blockage
Don’t:
Use cotton swabs, bobby pins, or sharp tools
Attempt DIY ear irrigation without medical advice
Insert anything deep into your ear canal
Ignore symptoms like pain, hearing loss, or discharge
What’s the Best Way to Remove Ear Wax?
The best method depends on your situation. If you’re not having any symptoms, it’s usually best to clean only the outer ear and let the ear canal’s natural self-cleaning process do its job.
For mild wax buildup, softening drops or gentle irrigation may help in some cases, but these should be used carefully and ideally with professional guidance.

If the wax is impacted, keeps coming back, or is causing symptoms like fullness, muffled hearing, or discomfort, the safest next step is to see a hearing specialist or medical provider for an evaluation.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we can help determine whether earwax may be affecting your hearing and guide you on the safest next steps for care.
Listen to Your Ears

Ear wax isn’t your enemy. It’s actually your body’s way of protecting your ears. The real danger lies in trying to clean your ears the wrong way. Misusing cotton swabs or inserting objects into your ears can cause damage that’s far worse than a little wax.
If you’re experiencing symptoms of cerumen impaction or just want peace of mind, the safest thing you can do is schedule a visit with a hearing professional.
Audiologists at Roberts Hearing Clinic are ready to help you take care of your ears the right way.
Don’t risk your hearing, trust only the experts.
Call Roberts Hearing Clinic to schedule an appointment with expert audiologists in Alexandria, LA!

children.text: Home » Hearing » Ear Candles: Do They Really Work?
Ear Candles: Do They Really Work?
Julie Tucker
February 15, 2025
Hearing

You may have seen ear candles at local health stores or online and wondered if they really help with earwax removal. These products claim to “suck out” wax and toxins using heat and suction—but are they safe or effective?
In truth, ear wax is a healthy and protective part of your ear’s natural cleaning system. Trying to remove it the wrong way can actually cause injury or infection.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we want to help you protect your ears with expert advice and safe solutions.
Overview of Ear Candling

Ear candling involves placing a long, hollow candle in your ear and lighting the outer end. As the flame burns, it supposedly creates suction to pull out wax. But research shows that’s not what happens. What people often see inside the candle afterward is melted candle wax—not ear wax.
In fact, ear candling can push wax deeper into the canal or cause burns. Since earwax helps protect against dust, bacteria, and moisture, audiologists strongly discourage this method.
How Are Ear Candles Used?

Typically about 10 inches long and made of waxed cloth, ear candles are lit while one end is placed in the ear. The user lies on their side, and the candle burns for several minutes. While some claim this draws wax out, what’s actually left inside the candle is usually just residue from the candle itself. Not only is this method ineffective, but it can also be dangerous—leading to burns, blockages, or even punctured eardrums.
What Do Experts Say About Ear Candling?

Hearing health professionals warn against using ear candles. Studies show they do not effectively remove wax, and the risks far outweigh any possible benefit. Common injuries include candle wax dripping into the ear, burns on the skin, and worsened blockages.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we’ve seen firsthand how harmful these products can be.
Audiologists recommend safer alternatives backed by science, not myths. There are far better ways to protect your hearing and maintain ear health without putting yourself at risk.
What Does the FDA Say About Ear Candles?

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued several warnings about the use of ear candles. These products are considered unapproved medical devices, and the FDA prohibits companies from marketing them as earwax removal tools.

According to the agency, ear candles can lead to serious injuries such as burns, punctured eardrums, and even temporary hearing loss. The FDA continues to caution consumers against using them and urges people to seek professional ear care instead.
How Can I Remove Wax Safely?
Most of the time, ear wax doesn’t need to be removed. It naturally moves out of the ear on its own. But if you’re experiencing blockage, pressure, or hearing changes, it’s time to see an audiologist.
Audiologists offer safe and professional wax removal using gentle tools and techniques. While over-the-counter drops can help soften wax, at-home methods like ear candles can do more harm than good.
Trusting your hearing to a trained expert is always the best approach.
What Are Safer Methods to Clean Our Ears?
Safe ear care doesn’t require risky tools or home remedies. Try these doctor-recommended tips:
Use a warm, damp washcloth to clean only the outer ear.
Avoid cotton swabs or anything inserted into the ear canal.
Use wax-softening drops if recommended by your audiologist.
Schedule professional cleanings if you experience frequent buildup or discomfort.
Your ears are naturally self-cleaning, so most people do not need to do anything to remove wax on their own.

If you are unsure whether wax is affecting your hearing, or if you are dealing with fullness, muffled sound, or discomfort, the team at Roberts Hearing Clinic in Alexandria, LA can help by evaluating your hearing and checking for possible ear-related concerns.
We provide hearing evaluations, guidance on safe ear care, and support to help you understand the next best step for your ear and hearing health.
Audiologists in Alexandria, LA

Ear candling may seem like a simple, natural fix, but it’s not safe, and it doesn’t work. Leading medical experts and the FDA agree: ear candles can cause burns, worsen wax problems, and even damage your hearing.
Instead of taking that risk, turn to a trusted audiologist for proper care.
Roberts Hearing Clinic connects you to expert audiologists in Alexandria, LA. We offer personalized hearing care to keep your ears healthy and protected.
Call us today to schedule your visit and hear with confidence.

children.text: Home » Tinnitus » Hearing Aids for Tinnitus
Hearing Aids for Tinnitus
Julie Tucker
March 15, 2025
Tinnitus

If you hear a ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound in your ears that others can’t hear, you may be experiencing tinnitus. For many people, this phantom sound can be a daily source of distraction or discomfort.
While tinnitus can have many causes—such as loud noise exposure, hearing loss, or certain medical conditions—it often goes hand-in-hand with hearing issues.

The good news is that there are ways to manage tinnitus, and hearing aids are one of the most effective options available. These small devices don’t just improve your hearing—they can also reduce the intensity and impact of tinnitus. By helping you hear real sounds more clearly, hearing aids can shift your focus away from the noise inside your head.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we understand how frustrating tinnitus can be. We take a personalized approach to care and offer solutions that are designed to improve your hearing and overall quality of life.
If you’re struggling with ringing in your ears, hearing aids might be the answer.
We provide hearing solutions, including hearing aids for tinnitus in Alexandria, LA.
Why Choose Hearing Aids for Tinnitus?
Hearing aids offer several important benefits for those experiencing tinnitus:
Tinnitus Masking : Many hearing aids include sound therapy features that play soft background sounds to cover up the tinnitus.
Auditory Enrichment : Amplifying the sounds around you makes the tinnitus less noticeable.
Improved Focus and Sleep : Less attention on the ringing means better rest and concentration.
Reduced Stress : Lower stress levels can help reduce how strongly tinnitus is perceived.
Dual Purpose : They treat hearing loss and provide relief for tinnitus at the same time.
Masking and Attentional Effects

Modern hearing aids often come with built-in masking features, such as soft tones or white noise. These sounds can reduce the contrast between the tinnitus and quiet environments, making the ringing less noticeable. They also help shift your brain’s focus away from the internal noise and toward real-world sounds.
Auditory Stimulation

By amplifying ambient sounds, hearing aids provide constant auditory input that can help retrain your brain to pay less attention to the tinnitus. This consistent stimulation reduces the brain’s tendency to “fill in the silence” with phantom noises.
Improved Communication

Tinnitus and hearing loss often occur together, making conversations more difficult and frustrating. Hearing aids can greatly improve your ability to understand speech, especially in noisy settings, reducing the need to strain or guess during conversations.

More importantly, working with an audiologist ensures that your tinnitus is properly assessed and addressed. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we provide customized hearing aid fittings and tinnitus counseling to help you better understand your condition. Patient education and support are essential in managing tinnitus, and our team is here to guide you through every step of the process.
The Link Between Hearing Loss and Ringing in the Ears

Tinnitus and hearing loss are closely connected. When the auditory system is damaged—whether from age, noise exposure, or other causes—it can reduce the brain’s access to sound. In response, the brain may “create” sound in the form of ringing or buzzing to fill in the gaps.

In fact, studies show that about 80% of people with tinnitus also have some degree of hearing loss. Because of this overlap, hearing aids are often one of the most effective treatments. They don’t just make speech and other sounds more audible—they also reduce the perception of tinnitus by giving the brain real sounds to focus on.

Additionally, hearing aids can improve mental health by decreasing the emotional burden of tinnitus. Less frustration and fatigue from strained communication can improve mood, reduce anxiety, and enhance your overall quality of life.
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides hearing aids in Alexandria, LA.
Selecting the Best Hearing Aids for Tinnitus

Choosing the right hearing aids depends on your specific hearing profile and the severity of your tinnitus. Many advanced devices include tinnitus-specific features like customizable sound generators, Bluetooth streaming for sound therapy apps, and automatic volume adjustments.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we help you select a device that meets your hearing and tinnitus relief needs. Our Alexandria, LA audiologists perform a thorough evaluation, explain your options clearly, and fine-tune your hearing aids for the best results.
We will help you compare styles, features, and price points to find what’s right for you.
Hearing Aids for Tinnitus in Alexandria, LA

If you’re living with constant ringing in your ears, you don’t have to suffer in silence. Roberts Hearing Clinic offers advanced hearing aids for tinnitus in Alexandria, LA, along with expert support from licensed audiologists.
We’re committed to helping you improve your hearing and reduce the impact of tinnitus on your daily life.
Schedule a consultation today!

Normal Hearing Range: What Your Hearing Test Results Mean
Julie Tucker
April 25, 2026
Hearing
Normal hearing range usually means you can hear very soft sounds across the main speech frequencies without needing extra volume.
A hearing test measures hearing thresholds in decibels and frequencies, then plots the results on an audiogram.
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides hearing evaluations, diagnostic testing, and follow-up care in Alexandria, LA, for patients who want to understand their hearing clearly.
What Is the Normal Hearing Range?

Normal hearing range describes the softest sounds a person can hear across different pitches. On a standard hearing test, this is measured in decibels hearing level, written as dB HL. Many audiology references consider hearing thresholds around -10 to 15 dB HL to be within the normal range. Some clinical explanations also use 0 to 20 or 0 to 25 dB HL as a practical normal range for adults.

That difference can be confusing, but the main idea is simple: the closer your hearing thresholds are to the top of the audiogram, the softer the sounds you can hear. Higher numbers on the audiogram mean louder sounds are needed before you detect them.

Normal hearing does not mean every sound is comfortable or easy to understand in every setting. You can have normal hearing thresholds and still struggle in background noise, with fast talkers, with tinnitus, or with sound sensitivity. A hearing test helps separate normal threshold sensitivity from other listening concerns.
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides comprehensive hearing tests in Alexandria, LA and nearby communities.
How Hearing Range Is Measured
A professional hearing evaluation usually measures how softly you can hear tones at different pitches. These results are plotted on an audiogram.
Decibels Measure Loudness
Decibels describe sound level. In hearing testing, dB HL does not mean the same thing as the everyday environmental sound level. It is a scale designed for hearing tests.
On an audiogram, lower numbers mean softer sounds. For example, hearing a tone at 10 dB HL is better sensitivity than hearing that same tone only at 40 dB HL.
Frequencies Measure Pitch

Frequencies are measured in hertz, written as Hz. Low frequencies are deeper sounds, such as a bass voice or a low drum. High frequencies are sharper sounds, such as birds, consonants, and many speech details.

Most standard hearing tests check several frequencies important for speech, often from low pitches through high pitches. Your results may be normal at some pitches and outside the normal range at others.
Thresholds Show the Softest Sound You Can Hear

A threshold is the softest level at which you can detect a sound at a specific frequency. If your threshold at 2000 Hz is 10 dB HL, that means you heard a very soft tone at that pitch. If your threshold at 4000 Hz is 45 dB HL, you need a louder tone to hear that pitch.

The pattern of your thresholds matters as much as the numbers. A person may have normal low-frequency hearing and high-frequency hearing loss, which can make speech sound muffled even when the volume seems loud enough.
Normal Hearing Range on an Audiogram

An audiogram is a chart. Frequencies run from left to right, from low pitch to high pitch. Loudness runs from top to bottom, from soft to loud. This can feel upside down at first because better hearing appears closer to the top of the chart.
In general:
Normal hearing is often around -10 to 15 dB HL.
Slight hearing loss is often around 16 to 25 dB HL.
Mild hearing loss is often around 26 to 40 dB HL.
Moderate hearing loss is often around 41 to 55 dB HL.
Moderately severe hearing loss is often around 56 to 70 dB HL.
Severe hearing loss is often around 71 to 90 dB HL.
Profound hearing loss is often 91 dB HL or greater.

Your audiologist may explain your results using slightly different cutoffs depending on your age, symptoms, test method, and clinical context. The category is helpful, but your real-world listening experience matters too.
What Frequencies Matter Most for Speech?
Speech uses a range of frequencies. Vowels tend to carry more low-frequency energy, while many consonants use higher frequencies. Consonants such as s, f, th, sh, and t help make words clear.

This is why high-frequency hearing loss can be frustrating. You may hear that someone is talking but miss the exact words. You may also have more trouble with children’s voices, soft speakers, speech in noise, or conversations from another room.

A normal hearing range across speech frequencies usually supports clearer communication. But if one part of the range drops, speech can become less crisp even if your hearing is normal at other pitches.
Is 0 dB Perfect Hearing?
No. On a hearing test, 0 dB HL does not mean there is no sound. It means the sound is at a reference level based on average normal hearing sensitivity.
Some people can hear certain tones below 0 dB HL, such as -5 or -10 dB HL. That does not mean they have superhuman hearing. It simply means they heard softer-than-reference tones at that frequency.

Likewise, a threshold of 20 dB HL may still be considered normal or near normal in many adult clinical settings, but it may be meaningful if you are having symptoms or if the result is different from your previous test.
What Is a Normal Hearing Range by Age?

Hearing can change with age, but age-related change is not the same as healthy hearing. Many adults gradually lose sensitivity to high-frequency sounds. That can make speech clarity harder, especially in background noise.

Children are often expected to have very sensitive hearing because even slight hearing difficulty can affect speech, learning, and listening effort. Adults may still function well with small threshold shifts, but changes should be monitored if they affect communication.

If you are asking whether your hearing is normal for your age, a better question may be: are your results normal enough for the way you live, work, communicate, and stay safe? A hearing evaluation can help answer that more clearly than a general age chart.
Can You Have Normal Hearing and Still Have Trouble Hearing?
Yes. A standard audiogram is important, but it does not measure every listening skill. You may have normal hearing thresholds and still struggle with:
Background noise
Tinnitus
Sound sensitivity
Listening fatigue
Auditory processing concerns
Ear pressure or fullness
Trouble following fast speech
Difficulty hearing accents or soft voices

If your audiogram is normal but your symptoms are real, tell your audiologist where you struggle. Speech-in-noise testing, middle ear testing, tinnitus evaluation, or additional counseling may help explain what is happening.
What If One Ear Is Normal and the Other Is Not?

A difference between ears can matter. Even if one ear falls in the normal range, the other ear may have hearing loss that affects sound direction, balance between ears, and speech understanding in noise.

You should schedule a professional evaluation if one ear seems worse than the other, if hearing changes suddenly, or if hearing loss comes with dizziness, ear pain, drainage, pressure, or ringing in one ear.
Sudden hearing changes should be treated as urgent. Do not wait to see whether they improve on their own.
When Does Hearing Loss Start?
Hearing loss begins when your thresholds move outside the expected normal range. But the impact depends on which frequencies are affected and how much listening difficulty you notice.

Mild hearing loss can still cause real problems. You may miss soft speech, parts of a conversation, or speech in background noise. Moderate hearing loss can make everyday conversation harder without amplification. More severe hearing loss may require stronger hearing technology and additional communication support.
This is why the audiogram is only part of the picture. Your audiologist should also ask about your daily listening needs.
Does Normal Hearing Mean You Do Not Need Hearing Aids?

If your hearing thresholds are truly within the normal range, hearing aids are usually not recommended for hearing loss. However, some people with normal thresholds may need help with tinnitus, sound sensitivity, communication strategies, hearing protection, or further testing.

If your hearing test shows hearing loss, hearing aids may be discussed depending on the type and degree of loss, your speech understanding, and your communication goals. A hearing aid fitting is a separate step after the evaluation. It uses your test results to program devices for your hearing needs.
Common Questions About Normal Hearing Range
What is considered normal hearing in db?

Normal hearing is commonly described as thresholds around -10 to 15 dB HL. Some adult hearing-test explanations use up to 20 or 25 dB HL as a practical normal or near-normal cutoff. Your audiologist can explain which range applies to your results.
What is a normal hearing frequency range?

The human ear can detect a wide range of pitches, but clinical hearing tests focus on the frequencies most useful for communication. These often include low, mid, and high frequencies related to speech understanding.
Is mild hearing loss a big deal?

It can be. Mild hearing loss may not seem serious on paper, but it can affect soft speech, speech in noise, and listening effort. If you feel like people mumble or you often ask for repetition, mild hearing loss may be more noticeable than the name suggests.
Can online hearing tests tell me my normal range?

Online hearing tests may give a rough screening, but they cannot replace a diagnostic hearing evaluation. Headphones, background noise, device volume, and calibration all affect results. If you want to know your actual hearing thresholds, schedule a professional hearing test.
How often should adults have their hearing checked?

Adults should consider a baseline hearing test, then repeat testing if they notice changes, have tinnitus, work around noise, have a history of ear problems, or struggle in conversation. Your provider can recommend a schedule based on your results and risk factors.

Pressure in the Ear: Causes, Care, and When to See an Audiologist
Julie Tucker
January 8, 2025
Hearing

Have you ever had that stuffed-up ear feeling—like you’re underwater or your ears just won’t “pop”? That uncomfortable sensation is known as ear pressure , and it can feel like fullness, tightness, or even dull aching in the ear. You might also notice muffled hearing, pain, dizziness, or ringing.

While it’s often temporary and harmless, persistent or recurring ear pressure can indicate something more serious. Because the ear is a complex system connected to the throat, sinuses, and jaw, any disruption can affect how it feels or functions. That’s why getting it checked out by a professional is so important.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic , our audiologists in Alexandria, LA are trained to evaluate ear-related symptoms and help you find the right care to protect your hearing and comfort.
What Causes Pressure in the Ear?
1. Ear Wax Buildup

One of the most common reasons for ear pressure is a blockage caused by ear wax. While cerumen (earwax) helps protect your ears, too much of it can build up and block the canal. This can create a feeling of pressure, reduce hearing, or even lead to infection.
Trying to remove it with cotton swabs often makes things worse. For safe, effective relief, it’s best to have wax removed professionally.
Roberts Hearing Clinic offers ear wax removal in Alexandria, LA to help clear blockages and restore comfort.
2. Eustachian Tube Dysfunction

The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ears to your throat and help equalize pressure. If these tubes get blocked—by allergies, sinus infections, or colds—pressure builds up, causing that clogged-ear sensation or a “popping” feeling.
Chronic Eustachian tube dysfunction may need ongoing management and professional evaluation to avoid long-term effects on hearing and comfort.
3. Middle Ear Infections (Otitis Media)
Ear pressure can also result from fluid buildup due to infection in the middle ear. These infections are more common in children but can affect adults—especially after upper respiratory infections.
If left untreated, ear infections can damage hearing. If you experience frequent pain or fullness in your ears, it’s time for an expert evaluation.
4. Barotrauma

Changes in altitude—like flying, scuba diving, or mountain driving—can make your ears feel blocked or painful. This is called barotrauma, and it occurs when the air pressure in your middle ear doesn’t equalize quickly enough.
Usually, the discomfort goes away on its own, but lingering symptoms after travel may require medical attention.
5. Meniere’s Disease

A chronic condition called Meniere’s disease causes pressure in the inner ear, often with dizziness, ringing (tinnitus), and hearing loss. This fluid imbalance affects balance and hearing, and early care is key to managing symptoms.
6. Other Causes
Additional conditions linked to ear pressure include:
Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders
Structural issues in the ear canal
Growths or benign tumors like acoustic neuromas
Each case is unique—seeing an audiologist ensures the correct diagnosis and treatment path.
Why You Should See an Audiologist for Ear Pressure
1. Accurate Diagnosis
Our audiologists can perform detailed ear inspections and hearing tests to determine what’s causing the pressure. Whether it’s wax, fluid, or inflammation, we’ll help identify the issue.
2. Personalized Care

Not every ear problem needs the same solution. We tailor our care plans to your specific symptoms—whether it’s removing wax, advising on Eustachian tube exercises, or referring you to an ENT for medical treatment.
3. Ongoing Hearing Support
If your ear pressure is affecting your hearing, we can monitor your hearing levels and recommend appropriate assistive devices when needed.
4. Follow-Up Care and Consultations
Our care doesn’t stop after your first visit. We’re committed to helping you manage ear discomfort and protect your hearing long-term.
Common Treatments for Ear Pressure
Professional Ear Wax Removal We safely remove ear wax using specialized tools that won’t damage your ear canal.
Supportive Treatments for Infections If your symptoms suggest an infection, we can work with your physician to ensure you get the right medication, like antibiotics or decongestants.
Hearing Aids for Chronic Conditions If chronic conditions like Meniere’s disease are present, we offer hearing aids and support to improve your daily hearing experience.
Surgical Referrals In some cases—like fluid buildup that won’t resolve—we may refer you to an ENT for procedures like placing tubes in the ear.
When to Seek Immediate Help
Don’t wait to seek help if you experience:
Sudden, sharp ear pain
Quick onset of hearing loss
Dizziness or vertigo
Ongoing tinnitus
Fluid or pus draining from the ear
These may signal a more serious issue. Prompt attention helps prevent permanent damage.
How to Prevent Ear Pressure
Avoid cotton swabs They often push wax deeper and can cause irritation or injury.
Equalize pressure during travel Yawning, chewing gum, or using filtered earplugs can help prevent barotrauma during flights or elevation changes.
Treat allergies and sinus issues promptly Keeping your sinuses and Eustachian tubes clear reduces the chance of pressure buildup.
Schedule regular ear checkups Preventative care can catch issues before they worsen.
Consult With Audiologists in Alexandria, LA
If you’re struggling with uncomfortable ear pressure, don’t ignore the symptoms. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, our team is here to help you find relief and preserve your hearing health.
With expert evaluation, safe ear wax removal, and personalized hearing care, we’ll guide you every step of the way.
Call today or fill out our online form to schedule your appointment with an expert audiologist in Alexandria, LA.

Rechargeable Hearing Aids: A Simple, Convenient Solution for Better Hearing
Julie Tucker
February 27, 2025
Hearing Aid

Rechargeable hearing aids are quickly becoming one of the most popular options for individuals with hearing loss. Instead of using small, disposable batteries that need frequent replacement, these modern devices are powered by built-in rechargeable batteries—offering a more convenient and eco-friendly solution. With just a simple overnight charge, users can enjoy all-day hearing without the hassle of changing batteries.

Roberts Hearing Clinic helps you discover how these devices can simplify your daily routine and enhance your hearing experience. We offer a wide selection of rechargeable hearing aids in Alexandria, LA.
How Rechargeable Hearing Aids Work

Rechargeable hearing aids use built-in lithium-ion batteries, similar to those found in smartphones. These batteries are designed for long-term use and provide consistent power throughout the day. Most models come with a charging station where users simply place their hearing aids overnight or during short breaks.
There’s no need to handle tiny battery doors or carry extra batteries around. It’s a plug-and-play experience that makes hearing easier and more accessible.
Benefits of Rechargeable Hearing Aids
Convenience: No more buying or changing tiny disposable batteries.
Environmentally Friendly: Helps reduce the amount of battery waste in landfills.
Cost-Effective: Saves money over time by eliminating the need for frequent battery purchases.
Long Battery Life: Many models offer up to 24 hours of power on a single charge.
Easy Charging: Most users adopt a simple overnight routine, while others benefit from quick-charge options for busy days.
These benefits make rechargeable hearing aids an excellent choice for both new and experienced hearing aid users.
Who Can Benefit From Rechargeable Hearing Aids?
Rechargeable hearing aids are perfect for:
People looking for a low-maintenance hearing solution
Individuals with mild to profound hearing loss
Seniors or anyone with arthritis, tremors, or poor vision
Busy individuals who want easy charging and fewer accessories to manage
If you value simplicity and reliability, rechargeable hearing aids might be the best option for you.
FAQs About Rechargeable Hearing Aids
How long does the battery last?
Most devices offer a full day of use (16-30 hours) on a single charge, depending on usage and model.
How often do I need to charge my hearing aids?
It’s best to charge them every night, just like a smartphone.
What if I forget to charge them?
Many hearing aids come with quick-charge features, giving several hours of power in just 15–30 minutes.
Are rechargeable hearing aids water-resistant?
Yes, most modern models are water- and sweat-resistant, but not waterproof. They can handle everyday moisture.
What happens when the battery eventually wears out?
Rechargeable batteries typically last 3–5 years. When needed, the battery can be replaced by your audiologist or sent to the manufacturer.
Rechargeable Hearing Aids in Alexandria, LA

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we specialize in fitting and maintaining rechargeable hearing aids for all levels of hearing loss. Our team in Alexandria, LA provides personalized care, helping you choose the right device for your lifestyle.
Whether you’re new to hearing aids or ready to upgrade from traditional batteries, we’re here to guide you every step of the way.
Contact Roberts Hearing Clinic to schedule your consultation or hearing test in Alexandria, LA.
Let us help you find a hearing solution that fits your life—simple, modern, and worry-free.

Should You Trust an Online Hearing Test?
Julie Tucker
April 30, 2025
Hearing

In today’s digital world, many health checks can be done from the comfort of your home—including hearing tests. A quick internet search will reveal dozens of free online hearing tests promising fast results. While these tests can be helpful as a starting point, they are not a substitute for a professional evaluation.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we believe your hearing deserves more than a screen-based guess. Whether you’re curious about your hearing health or experiencing actual symptoms, nothing compares to a comprehensive hearing test conducted by a licensed audiologist.
We provide comprehensive hearing tests in Alexandria, LA.
How Accurate Are Online Hearing Tests?

Online hearing tests typically play a series of tones at different pitches and volumes, asking you to respond when you hear a sound. Some tests also include speech recognition in noisy backgrounds. While these tools can give you a general idea of how well you hear, they have limitations.

Online tests rely on your device’s sound settings, the quality of your headphones, and your surrounding environment—all of which can impact accuracy. They don’t measure bone conduction, inner ear function, or detect potential causes of hearing loss like ear wax buildup or ear infections.
So while online tests may flag a potential issue, they are not medically reliable for diagnosis or treatment planning.
Do Online Hearing Tests Work?

In short, they work to a degree. Online hearing tests can serve as screening tools. If you notice that you’re struggling with certain pitches or can’t hear voices clearly during the test, it’s a good indicator that you may need to see an audiologist. However, online tests do not replace the expertise of a trained professional.
They can alert you to possible issues, but should never be used as the final word on your hearing health.
What Are the Benefits of Online Hearing Tests?
Despite their limitations, online hearing tests do offer some clear advantages:
Convenience : You can take them anytime, anywhere—no appointment needed.
Accessibility : Free tests lower the barrier to entry for people curious about their hearing.
Early Awareness : They can serve as a helpful first step in identifying potential hearing problems.
Motivation : Some people may be hesitant to visit a clinic, so taking an online test might encourage them to seek professional help after noticing a problem.
These benefits make online hearing tests a good starting point, but they should not be your only step.
Pros and Cons of Online Hearing Tests
Pros:
Quick and easy to use
Free or low-cost
Great for raising awareness
Can be taken in the privacy of your home
Cons:
Results are not clinically accurate
No insight into the cause of hearing loss
Cannot diagnose medical conditions
Highly dependent on device quality and quiet surroundings
Might give false confidence or unnecessary worry
An online test may tell you if you have a hearing issue, but only a trained audiologist can tell you why —and what to do about it.
Roberts Hearing Clinic connects you to expert audiologists in Alexandria, LA.
Hearing Tests in Alexandria, LA

If you’re in Alexandria or the surrounding Central Louisiana region, your best choice for hearing care is Roberts Hearing Clinic. We provide comprehensive, professional hearing evaluations in a friendly, comfortable setting.
Unlike online tests, we use advanced diagnostic equipment to test air and bone conduction, speech recognition, and more.

Our audiologists can help you determine not only whether you have hearing loss, but also the type, cause, and best course of treatment—whether that’s hearing aids, wax removal, or medical referral. We’ll guide you every step of the way.
Contact us today to schedule a hearing test in Alexandria, LA!

Swimmer’s Ear: Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
Julie Tucker
April 4, 2025
Hearing

Swimmer’s ear, medically known as otitis externa, is an infection of the outer ear canal—the passage that leads from the outer ear to the eardrum. It’s commonly caused by water getting trapped in the ear after swimming, but it can also develop from moisture or irritation due to other factors.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we help patients understand, diagnose, and treat swimmer’s ear so they can get back to feeling comfortable and hearing clearly. Whether you’re an avid swimmer or simply prone to ear irritation, our audiologists in Alexandria, LA, are ready to support your ear health with expert care.
What Causes Swimmer’s Ear?
Swimmer’s ear typically develops when water becomes trapped in the ear canal, creating a moist environment that allows bacteria or fungi to grow. But it can also be triggered by:
Excessive cleaning that removes protective earwax
Damage to the skin in the ear canal (from cotton swabs, hearing aids, or fingernails)
Exposure to allergens or harsh chemicals like hair products or chlorine
These conditions compromise the ear’s natural defenses and make it more vulnerable to infection.
The Ear’s Natural Defenses

Your ears are naturally equipped to protect themselves. Cerumen, or ear wax, acts as a barrier by repelling water, trapping dust and debris, and preventing the growth of harmful bacteria. The shape of the ear canal and the slight downward angle also help water drain out naturally.

However, when this balance is disturbed by over-cleaning, excessive moisture, or irritation, these defenses break down. Without sufficient wax or if the skin becomes damaged, the ear canal becomes a perfect home for bacteria or fungi to thrive, leading to swimmer’s ear.
Why Do People Get Swimmer’s Ear?
Several things can trigger swimmer’s ear, including:
Excess moisture : Swimming, bathing, or sweating can cause water to collect in the ear canal.
Scratches or abrasions : Using cotton swabs or fingernails can create tiny cuts that allow bacteria in.
Sensitivity reactions : Hair sprays, shampoos, or jewelry can irritate the ear and increase infection risk.
What Are the Signs of Swimmer’s Ear?
Mild signs and symptoms:
Itching inside the ear canal
Slight redness
Mild discomfort that increases when pulling the ear
Moderate progression:
Increased pain
More noticeable redness
Discharge of fluid or pus
Feeling of fullness in the ear
Advanced progression:
Severe pain spreading to the face, neck, or head
Blocked or muffled hearing
Swollen lymph nodes
Fever
How Is Swimmer’s Ear Treated?
Treatment depends on the severity of the infection but typically includes:
Prescription ear drops containing antibiotics, antifungals, or steroids
Ear cleaning by a healthcare provider to remove debris or discharge
Pain relievers for comfort
Keeping the ear dry during recovery
Most cases clear up within 7–10 days when treated promptly and properly.
Can Swimmer’s Ear Be Prevented?
Yes! Here are some easy ways to reduce your risk:
Keep your ears dry: Use a towel after swimming or showering, and tilt your head to help water drain.
Use swim earplugs or a swim cap to protect ears during water activities.
Avoid inserting objects into your ears, including cotton swabs.
Protect your ears from irritants, such as hair sprays or harsh shampoos.
Be cautious if you’ve recently had an ear infection or injury—wait until your ear has fully healed before swimming again.
Swimmer’s Ear Risk Factors
You may be at higher risk for swimmer’s ear if you:
Swim frequently or dive regularly
Live in a hot, humid climate
Have a narrow or hairy ear canal
Use hearing aids or earbuds often
Have skin conditions like eczema or psoriasis
Clean your ears aggressively
Swimmer’s Ear: Complications
When untreated or recurring, swimmer’s ear can lead to:
Temporary hearing loss due to blockage or inflammation
Chronic otitis externa, which may persist or keep returning
Cellulitis, a deeper infection that can spread to nearby skin tissues
Bone and cartilage damage in the ear canal
Spread of infection to the skull base, cranial nerves, or even the brain in rare, severe cases
These complications are uncommon but highlight the importance of early treatment and proper care.
Conclusion
Swimmer’s ear may start off mild, but it can quickly become painful and disruptive. If you’re experiencing ear discomfort, drainage, or hearing changes, it’s best to get checked by a professional.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we’re dedicated to protecting your ear health and restoring your comfort. Whether you swim often or just want to keep your ears in top shape, we’re here to help.
Schedule an appointment with expert audiologists in Alexandria, LA today!

Understanding Hyperacusis: Causes, Symptoms & Treatment
Julie Tucker
March 26, 2025
Hearing

Does the sound of everyday life—like clinking dishes, barking dogs, or even soft music—feel painfully loud or overwhelming? You might be experiencing a condition called hyperacusis, which is an increased sensitivity to normal sounds. This condition can impact your daily comfort, communication, and quality of life.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we understand how frustrating and isolating hyperacusis can be. In this blog, we’ll explore the signs, causes, and treatment options so you can better manage your symptoms and find relief.
Hyperacusis: Signs and Symptoms
Hyperacusis doesn’t just mean you dislike loud noise—it means your brain is reacting to sound in a way that feels physically painful or emotionally distressing.
People with hyperacusis often describe:
Sharp discomfort or pain when hearing normal sounds
Anxiety or stress in noisy environments
Trouble sleeping due to background noise
Avoidance of social situations because of noise sensitivity
Tinnitus (ringing in the ears), which often co-occurs with hyperacusis

If these symptoms sound familiar, you’re not alone. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we’ve helped many patients better understand and manage their noise sensitivity. Don’t suffer in silence—help is available.
Hyperacusis: Causes

Hyperacusis can be triggered by many different factors. In some cases, it develops suddenly after a loud noise exposure, like a concert or gunshot. For others, it might happen gradually due to underlying health conditions.
Common causes include:
Noise-induced hearing damage
Head injuries or concussions
Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders
Migraines
Lyme disease or other infections
Neurological disorders
Side effects of medications
Emotional stress, anxiety, and depression can also make hyperacusis worse. Identifying the cause with the help of a hearing care professional can lead to better-targeted treatment.
Diagnosing Hyperacusis

Getting an accurate diagnosis is the first step toward relief. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, our expert audiologists in Alexandria, LA will review your health history, listen to your concerns, and perform specialized hearing tests.

Because hyperacusis is often linked to other auditory conditions like tinnitus or hearing loss, a full hearing evaluation is essential. We’re here to provide personalized care and help you take back control of your sound environment.
Hyperacusis Treatment
Treating hyperacusis depends on what’s causing it and how severe your symptoms are. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we may recommend:
Sound therapy using devices or apps to desensitize your ears to sound gradually
Counseling or Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to help manage emotional stress tied to noise
Tinnitus Retraining Therapy (TRT) if tinnitus is also present
Custom ear protection to reduce harmful sounds while avoiding complete silence, which can make symptoms worse
With professional support, many people find significant relief from hyperacusis.
Hyperacusis Home Remedies
While professional diagnosis and treatment are essential, some people try home remedies to ease hyperacusis symptoms. These methods may help, especially when combined with expert guidance.
1. Sound enrichment: Use soft background noise like a fan, white noise machine, or nature sounds to desensitize your hearing system over time. Avoid total silence.
2. Relaxation techniques: Stress can amplify your sound sensitivity. Try deep breathing, yoga, or guided meditation to help calm your nervous system.
3. Avoid triggers: If you’ve identified certain sounds that cause discomfort, avoid them when possible—but don’t eliminate all sound, as this can worsen the condition.
4. Limit caffeine and alcohol: These substances can irritate the auditory system in some people. Reducing them may help with both hyperacusis and tinnitus.

5. Ear protection with care: Use earplugs or noise-canceling headphones in especially loud environments, but avoid overusing them. Constant earplug use can make your ears more sensitive in the long run.
While these at-home approaches may help, it’s crucial to work with an audiologist to prevent worsening your symptoms.
Hyperacusis varies from person to person, and what works for one may not work for another.
Hyperacusis Risk Factors
Several factors may increase your risk of developing hyperacusis:
Exposure to loud noises: Frequent or sudden loud sounds—especially without ear protection—can damage hearing and lead to noise sensitivity.
Hearing loss or tinnitus: Many people with hyperacusis also have tinnitus or hearing damage.
Head injuries: Trauma to the brain or ear can affect how the auditory system processes sound.
Neurological conditions: Issues such as migraines or autism spectrum disorders have been linked to sound sensitivity.
Mental health conditions: Stress, anxiety, and depression may not directly cause hyperacusis but can worsen your response to sound.
Being aware of these risk factors can help you take proactive steps—like using hearing protection and seeking early treatment when needed.
Audiologists and Hearing Tests in Alexandria, LA

Living with hyperacusis can feel overwhelming, but you don’t have to face it alone. By understanding the causes, symptoms, and treatment options, you can take the first step toward comfort and confidence in everyday sound environments.

Roberts Hearing Clinic has audiologists in Alexandria, LA who can diagnose and manage hearing conditions like hyperacusis. Our compassionate team is ready to help you feel at ease again—without pain from everyday sounds.
Contact Roberts Hearing Clinic to schedule your hearing test in Alexandria, LA!

children.text: Home » Roberts Hearing Clinic Audiology Services
Roberts Hearing Clinic Audiology Services

Roberts Hearing Clinic provides expert hearing care to help you stay connected to the sounds that matter most. From comprehensive hearing evaluations to advanced hearing aid solutions, our Alexandria, LA audiologists are here to support your hearing health with personalized care.
Hearing Services in Alexandria, LA
Hearing Evaluations
Your journey to better hearing begins with a thorough assessment. Our audiologists use state-of-the-art testing to identify hearing loss and create customized solutions that fit your lifestyle.
Which hearing test is the best?
The best hearing test depends on your specific needs. A comprehensive hearing evaluation conducted by an audiologist is the most accurate way to assess your hearing. Common tests include:
Pure-tone audiometry – Measures your ability to hear different pitches and volumes.
Speech audiometry – Assesses how well you understand speech at various sound levels.
Tympanometry – Evaluates middle ear function and detects fluid buildup, infections, or eardrum issues.
Otoacoustic emissions (OAE) testing – Checks inner ear function, often used for newborns and children.
Auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing – Measures how the brain processes sound, typically used for neurological evaluations.
A professional hearing test provides the most reliable diagnosis and helps determine the best treatment options.
Can I test my own hearing?
You can do a basic self-check by paying attention to signs of hearing loss, such as:
Struggling to hear in noisy environments
Frequently asking others to repeat themselves
Turning up the volume on the TV or phone
Difficulty hearing high-pitched voices

There are also smartphone apps and hearing test kits that provide a general idea of your hearing ability. However, these are not a substitute for a professional hearing evaluation and may not detect all types of hearing loss. If you suspect hearing problems, an audiologist can perform a thorough assessment to determine the best course of action.
Are online hearing tests any good?
Online hearing tests can be a helpful starting point, but they have limitations. They typically measure your ability to hear certain tones through headphones or speakers, but they cannot:
Diagnose the type or severity of hearing loss
Assess speech comprehension or middle ear function
Identify underlying medical conditions that may affect hearing

Since background noise, device quality, and calibration can affect results, online tests should only be used for a general screening. If an online test suggests hearing difficulties, it’s best to schedule a professional hearing evaluation with an audiologist for an accurate diagnosis and personalized solutions.
Diagnostic Services
We provide in-depth diagnostic testing to evaluate hearing health and detect any underlying conditions. Our team ensures precise results and guides you toward the best treatment options.
What are audiology diagnostic services, and why are they important?

Audiology diagnostic services include a range of tests used to assess hearing ability, ear health, and balance function. These evaluations help identify hearing loss, tinnitus, middle ear issues, and other auditory conditions. Accurate diagnosis allows audiologists to recommend the best treatment, whether it’s hearing aids, medical intervention, or specialized therapy.
What types of diagnostic tests are performed during a hearing evaluation?
A comprehensive hearing evaluation may include:
Pure-tone audiometry – Measures the softest sounds you can hear at different frequencies.
Speech audiometry – Evaluates how well you hear and understand speech in quiet and noisy environments.
Tympanometry – Tests middle ear function to detect fluid buildup, infections, or eardrum issues.
Otoacoustic emissions (OAE) – Assesses inner ear function, often used for newborns and young children.
Auditory brainstem response (ABR) – Evaluates how the brain processes sound, used for neurological assessments.
These tests help determine the type and severity of hearing loss and guide treatment options.
When should I get a diagnostic hearing test?
You should consider a diagnostic hearing test if you experience:
Difficulty hearing conversations, especially in noisy settings
Frequent ringing or buzzing in your ears ( tinnitus )
Muffled sounds or a sensation of fullness in the ears
Sudden or gradual hearing loss
Dizziness or balance issues
If you notice any of these symptoms, scheduling a hearing evaluation with an audiologist can help identify any hearing-related conditions and provide appropriate solutions.
Tinnitus Evaluations and Treatment

If you experience ringing or buzzing in your ears, our tinnitus evaluations can help determine the cause. We offer effective treatment options, including sound therapy and management strategies, to provide long-term relief.
Should I go to an audiologist for tinnitus?
Yes, an audiologist is one of the best professionals to help with tinnitus. If you’re experiencing ringing, buzzing, hissing, or other phantom sounds in your ears , an audiologist can:
Conduct a tinnitus evaluation to determine potential causes.
Check for underlying hearing loss , which is often linked to tinnitus.
Provide treatment options such as sound therapy, hearing aids with tinnitus masking, and relaxation techniques.
Offer coping strategies to help manage the effects of tinnitus on your daily life.
If tinnitus is interfering with your sleep, focus, or emotional well-being, seeing an audiologist can help you find relief and improve your quality of life.
Is tinnitus a brain problem?

Although tinnitus originates in the ears, it is often considered a neurological issue involving the brain’s auditory system. When the brain no longer receives certain sound signals due to hearing loss or ear damage, it may compensate by creating its own noise, which we perceive as tinnitus.

Because tinnitus is linked to brain activity, stress levels, and auditory processing, treatments focus on reducing perception rather than eliminating the sound completely. Techniques like sound therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and hearing aids can help the brain adjust and minimize tinnitus awareness.
What happens if tinnitus is not treated?
While tinnitus itself is not dangerous, leaving it unmanaged can lead to:
Increased stress, anxiety, or irritability
Difficulty concentrating or sleeping
Worsening hearing problems if linked to untreated hearing loss
Emotional distress , including frustration, depression, or social withdrawal
Ignoring tinnitus may make it feel more persistent and disruptive over time . Seeking professional help can help you better manage symptoms and prevent it from interfering with your daily life.
Hearing Aid Services

From choosing the right hearing aid to ongoing maintenance, we provide expert support every step of the way. Our services include fittings, adjustments, cleanings, and repairs to keep your hearing aids working at their best.
Hearing Aid Fittings
A well-fitted hearing aid ensures comfort and optimal sound quality. We customize your device for a seamless and natural listening experience, tailored to your specific hearing needs.
How long does it take to get fitted for a hearing aid?

The hearing aid fitting process typically takes about one to two hours. During this appointment, the audiologist will adjust the settings to match your hearing needs, ensure a comfortable fit, and teach you how to use and maintain your device. If a custom earmold is required, it may take an additional one to two weeks to be made before your final fitting. Follow-up visits are often scheduled to fine-tune the device for optimal performance.
How does an audiologist fit a hearing aid?
An audiologist fits a hearing aid through a step-by-step process to ensure the best sound quality and comfort:
Programming the device – The audiologist adjusts the hearing aid settings based on your hearing test results.
Ensuring proper fit – The hearing aid is placed in your ear and adjusted for a secure and comfortable fit.
Real-ear measurement (REM) – A small microphone measures how sound is amplified inside your ear canal, ensuring the device delivers the right level of amplification.
Testing and fine-tuning – You will listen to different sounds and speech to ensure clarity and comfort.
Providing instructions – The audiologist will show you how to insert, remove, clean, and maintain your hearing aids.
Scheduling follow-up adjustments – Additional visits may be needed to make further refinements based on your real-world listening experience.

  • Auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing – Measures how the brain processes sound, typically used for neurological evaluations.

 

A professional hearing test provides the most reliable diagnosis and helps determine the best treatment options.

Can I test my own hearing?

You can do a basic self-check by paying attention to signs of hearing loss, such as:

  • Struggling to hear in noisy environments
  • Frequently asking others to repeat themselves
  • Turning up the volume on the TV or phone
  • Difficulty hearing high-pitched voices

 

There are also smartphone apps and hearing test kits that provide a general idea of your hearing ability. However, these are not a substitute for a professional hearing evaluation and may not detect all types of hearing loss. If you suspect hearing problems, an audiologist can perform a thorough assessment to determine the best course of action.

Are online hearing tests any good?

Online hearing tests can be a helpful starting point, but they have limitations. They typically measure your ability to hear certain tones through headphones or speakers, but they cannot:

  • Diagnose the type or severity of hearing loss
  • Assess speech comprehension or middle ear function
  • Identify underlying medical conditions that may affect hearing

 

Since background noise, device quality, and calibration can affect results, online tests should only be used for a general screening. If an online test suggests hearing difficulties, it’s best to schedule a professional hearing evaluation with an audiologist for an accurate diagnosis and personalized solutions.

Diagnostic Services

We provide in-depth diagnostic testing to evaluate hearing health and detect any underlying conditions. Our team ensures precise results and guides you toward the best treatment options.

What are audiology diagnostic services, and why are they important?

Audiology diagnostic services include a range of tests used to assess hearing ability, ear health, and balance function. These evaluations help identify hearing loss, tinnitus, middle ear issues, and other auditory conditions. Accurate diagnosis allows audiologists to recommend the best treatment, whether it’s hearing aids, medical intervention, or specialized therapy.

What types of diagnostic tests are performed during a hearing evaluation?

A comprehensive hearing evaluation may include:

  • Pure-tone audiometry – Measures the softest sounds you can hear at different frequencies.
  • Speech audiometry – Evaluates how well you hear and understand speech in quiet and noisy environments.
  • Tympanometry – Tests middle ear function to detect fluid buildup, infections, or eardrum issues.
  • Otoacoustic emissions (OAE) – Assesses inner ear function, often used for newborns and young children.
  • Auditory brainstem response (ABR) – Evaluates how the brain processes sound, used for neurological assessments.

 

These tests help determine the type and severity of hearing loss and guide treatment options.

When should I get a diagnostic hearing test?

You should consider a diagnostic hearing test if you experience:

  • Difficulty hearing conversations, especially in noisy settings
  • Frequent ringing or buzzing in your ears (tinnitus)
  • Muffled sounds or a sensation of fullness in the ears
  • Sudden or gradual hearing loss
  • Dizziness or balance issues

 

If you notice any of these symptoms, scheduling a hearing evaluation with an audiologist can help identify any hearing-related conditions and provide appropriate solutions.

Tinnitus Evaluations and Treatment

If you experience ringing or buzzing in your ears, our tinnitus evaluations can help determine the cause. We offer effective treatment options, including sound therapy and management strategies, to provide long-term relief.

Should I go to an audiologist for tinnitus?

Yes, an audiologist is one of the best professionals to help with tinnitus. If you’re experiencing ringing, buzzing, hissing, or other phantom sounds in your ears, an audiologist can:

  • Conduct a tinnitus evaluation to determine potential causes.
  • Check for underlying hearing loss, which is often linked to tinnitus.
  • Provide treatment options such as sound therapy, hearing aids with tinnitus masking, and relaxation techniques.
  • Offer coping strategies to help manage the effects of tinnitus on your daily life.

 

If tinnitus is interfering with your sleep, focus, or emotional well-being, seeing an audiologist can help you find relief and improve your quality of life.

Is tinnitus a brain problem?

Although tinnitus originates in the ears, it is often considered a neurological issue involving the brain’s auditory system. When the brain no longer receives certain sound signals due to hearing loss or ear damage, it may compensate by creating its own noise, which we perceive as tinnitus.

Because tinnitus is linked to brain activity, stress levels, and auditory processing, treatments focus on reducing perception rather than eliminating the sound completely. Techniques like sound therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and hearing aids can help the brain adjust and minimize tinnitus awareness.

What happens if tinnitus is not treated?

While tinnitus itself is not dangerous, leaving it unmanaged can lead to:

  • Increased stress, anxiety, or irritability
  • Difficulty concentrating or sleeping
  • Worsening hearing problems if linked to untreated hearing loss
  • Emotional distress, including frustration, depression, or social withdrawal

 

Ignoring tinnitus may make it feel more persistent and disruptive over time. Seeking professional help can help you better manage symptoms and prevent it from interfering with your daily life.

Hearing Aid Services

From choosing the right hearing aid to ongoing maintenance, we provide expert support every step of the way. Our services include fittings, adjustments, cleanings, and repairs to keep your hearing aids working at their best.

Hearing Aid Fittings

A well-fitted hearing aid ensures comfort and optimal sound quality. We customize your device for a seamless and natural listening experience, tailored to your specific hearing needs.

How long does it take to get fitted for a hearing aid?

The hearing aid fitting process typically takes about one to two hours. During this appointment, the audiologist will adjust the settings to match your hearing needs, ensure a comfortable fit, and teach you how to use and maintain your device. If a custom earmold is required, it may take an additional one to two weeks to be made before your final fitting. Follow-up visits are often scheduled to fine-tune the device for optimal performance.

How does an audiologist fit a hearing aid?

An audiologist fits a hearing aid through a step-by-step process to ensure the best sound quality and comfort:

  1. Programming the device – The audiologist adjusts the hearing aid settings based on your hearing test results.
  2. Ensuring proper fit – The hearing aid is placed in your ear and adjusted for a secure and comfortable fit.
  3. Real-ear measurement (REM) – A small microphone measures how sound is amplified inside your ear canal, ensuring the device delivers the right level of amplification.
  4. Testing and fine-tuning – You will listen to different sounds and speech to ensure clarity and comfort.
  5. Providing instructions – The audiologist will show you how to insert, remove, clean, and maintain your hearing aids.
  6. Scheduling follow-up adjustments – Additional visits may be needed to make further refinements based on your real-world listening experience.

Can you get a hearing aid without a test?

Yes, over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids are available without a hearing test, but they are designed for mild to moderate hearing loss and do not offer the same level of customization as prescription hearing aids.

A professional hearing test ensures that you receive the right hearing aid for your specific needs. An audiologist can determine the type and severity of your hearing loss, program the device for optimal clarity, and rule out any medical conditions that may be affecting your hearing. If you’re unsure about your hearing needs, scheduling an evaluation with an audiologist is the best way to get the right solution.

Hearing Aid Repair

If your hearing aid isn’t functioning properly, our team provides fast and effective repairs. Whether it’s a simple adjustment or a more complex issue, we’re here to help.

What are common problems that require hearing aid repair?

Hearing aids can develop issues over time. Some common problems include:

  • No sound or low volume – May be due to a clogged wax filter, battery issues, or internal component failure.
  • Distorted or muffled sound – Can result from moisture buildup, microphone damage, or speaker problems.
  • Whistling or feedback noise – Often caused by a poor fit, earwax buildup, or malfunctioning components.
  • Physical damage – Cracked casings, broken battery doors, or loose parts may need professional repair.

How long does it take to repair a hearing aid?

The repair time depends on the issue. Simple fixes, like replacing a wax filter or cleaning the device, can often be done in-office within minutes. More complex repairs, such as internal component replacements, may require sending the hearing aid to the manufacturer, which can take several days to a few weeks.

Can I fix my hearing aid at home?

Some minor issues can be addressed at home, such as:

  • Replacing the battery
  • Cleaning the microphone, wax filter, and tubing
  • Checking volume settings and ensuring proper fit
  • Using a hearing aid dehumidifier to remove moisture

 

However, if the hearing aid still isn’t working properly, do not attempt to open or repair internal components yourself. This can cause further damage. Instead, consult your audiologist or hearing aid provider for professional repair.

Hearing Protection

Protecting your hearing is just as important as treating hearing loss. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we offer custom hearing protection for musicians, hunters, industrial workers, and anyone exposed to loud noise. Whether you need earplugs for concerts or in-ear monitors for work, we’ll help you find the perfect fit to keep your hearing safe-without sacrificing sound quality or comfort.

Why should I use hearing protection?

Loud sounds can damage your hearing over time, and once it’s gone, it can’t be reversed. Hearing protection helps reduce the risk of permanent hearing loss.

Are custom earplugs better than store-bought ones?

Yes. Custom earplugs are molded to your ears, so they fit better, feel more comfortable, and block out noise more effectively.

Can I still hear people talking with earplugs in?

Yes! Some earplugs are made to reduce harmful noise while still letting you hear speech clearly, which is perfect for work or social settings.

Tinnitus Support
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides expert tinnitus support in Alexandria, LA.

Tinnitus is a condition where you hear ringing, buzzing, hissing, or clicking sounds in your ears when there is no actual noise around you. It can be mild and occasional or persistent and disruptive, making it harder to focus, sleep, or enjoy daily activities.
What Causes Tinnitus?
Tinnitus can develop due to various factors, including:
Hearing loss – When the brain doesn’t receive normal sound input, it may create its own noises.
Exposure to loud sounds – Loud music, machinery, or concerts can damage hearing over time.
Earwax buildup – Too much earwax can block the ear canal and cause ringing.
Medications – Some drugs have tinnitus as a side effect.
Health conditions – Issues like high blood pressure, ear infections, and TMJ disorders can contribute to tinnitus.
Tinnitus Care Options
While there is no permanent cure for tinnitus, many treatments can help reduce symptoms and make it easier to live with.
Sound Therapy
Background noise can help mask tinnitus and make it less noticeable. Common options include:
White noise machines
Fans or soothing background music
Hearing aids with built-in sound masking
Hearing Aids
Lifestyle Changes
Everyday choices can also affect tinnitus. Certain habits may make symptoms worse, so it may help to:
Limit caffeine and alcohol
Use ear protection in noisy places
Practice relaxation exercises to reduce stress
Maintain a regular sleep routine
When to Seek More Care

While hearing aids and healthy lifestyle changes can be very effective, some people may need additional treatment. If symptoms persist or worsen, we may refer you to an ENT specialist for more comprehensive care.
Frequently Asked Questions About Tinnitus
Will tinnitus go away on its own?
Tinnitus may fade over time, especially if caused by a temporary issue like noise exposure or earwax buildup. However, if it lasts for weeks or worsens, seeing an audiologist is recommended.
Can stress make tinnitus worse?

Yes, stress and anxiety can increase tinnitus awareness. When your brain is stressed, it can become more sensitive to sounds, including internal ringing. Managing stress through relaxation techniques may help reduce symptoms.
Is tinnitus always linked to hearing loss?
Not always. While many people with tinnitus also have hearing loss, some with normal hearing still experience it. A hearing test can determine if hearing loss is a contributing factor.
Do hearing aids help with tinnitus?

Yes! Hearing aids can amplify external sounds, reducing the contrast between environmental sounds and tinnitus. Many also come with built-in tinnitus masking features that play soothing sounds to help distract from the ringing.
Can ear wax cause tinnitus?
Yes, excess earwax can block sound and cause ringing or buzzing in the ears. If earwax buildup is the cause, professional earwax removal can provide relief.
Tinnitus Support in Alexandria, LA
Our audiologist in Alexandria, LA, is here to help with expert tinnitus support and treatment options to make the ringing in your ears more manageable.
Call us today to schedule your tinnitus management!

Sound Therapy
