If you have hearing loss, using a hearing aid can improve overall sound clarity, which may make tinnitus less noticeable. Many hearing aids also include sound therapy features that provide gentle background tones to help reduce the focus on tinnitus. For many people, this combination of better hearing and additional sound support can make symptoms easier to manage.

Lifestyle Changes

Everyday choices can also affect tinnitus. Certain habits may make symptoms worse, so it may help to:

  • Limit caffeine and alcohol
  • Use ear protection in noisy places
  • Practice relaxation exercises to reduce stress
  • Maintain a regular sleep routine

 

When to Seek More Care

While hearing aids and healthy lifestyle changes can be very effective, some people may need additional treatment. If symptoms persist or worsen, we may refer you to an ENT specialist for more comprehensive care.

Frequently Asked Questions About Tinnitus

Will tinnitus go away on its own?

Tinnitus may fade over time, especially if caused by a temporary issue like noise exposure or earwax buildup. However, if it lasts for weeks or worsens, seeing an audiologist is recommended.

Can stress make tinnitus worse?

Yes, stress and anxiety can increase tinnitus awareness. When your brain is stressed, it can become more sensitive to sounds, including internal ringing. Managing stress through relaxation techniques may help reduce symptoms.

Is tinnitus always linked to hearing loss?

Not always. While many people with tinnitus also have hearing loss, some with normal hearing still experience it. A hearing test can determine if hearing loss is a contributing factor.

Do hearing aids help with tinnitus?

Yes! Hearing aids can amplify external sounds, reducing the contrast between environmental sounds and tinnitus. Many also come with built-in tinnitus masking features that play soothing sounds to help distract from the ringing.

Yes, excess earwax can block sound and cause ringing or buzzing in the ears. If earwax buildup is the cause, professional earwax removal can provide relief.

children.text: Home » Costco Hearing Aids
Costco Hearing Aids

Costco has become a popular destination for many shoppers, including those looking for hearing aids. Known for bulk deals and convenience, Costco offers hearing tests and hearing aids in many of its locations. While you don’t need to be a member to get your hearing tested, a Costco membership is required to purchase hearing aids.

They carry several well-known brands, including their own Kirkland Signature line, and offer features like Bluetooth streaming, rechargeable batteries, and smartphone compatibility. For some, the ability to pick up hearing aids while shopping for groceries is appealing.

But hearing loss isn’t just a shopping decision-it’s a medical issue. That’s why it’s so important to work with licensed audiologists who can guide you through the process with care, expertise, and personalized support.
Roberts Hearing Clinic connects you to expert audiologists and hearing aids in Alexandria, LA.
What Hearing Aids Does Costco Carry?
Costco offers hearing aids from brands such as:
Kirkland Signature (powered by Sonova)
Jabra Enhance (by ReSound)
Rexton (from the Signia family)
Philips HearLink

While these hearing aids may come at a lower price point, they are typically sold without the clinical care, in-depth fitting, and long-term support that patients receive at a private audiology clinic.
Hearing Aids at Roberts Hearing Clinic
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we offer hearing aids from many of the same top manufacturers-and a few more trusted names:
Phonak
ReSound
Widex
Oticon
Starkey
Unitron
Signia
Rexton
But the biggest difference vs. Costco? You’re never just buying a product-you’re receiving expert care.

Our audiologists take the time to understand your hearing needs, lifestyle, and budget. You’ll receive a complete diagnostic hearing evaluation, a custom fitting, and ongoing follow-up care to make sure your hearing aids perform at their best.
So… Is Costco a Good Place to Get Hearing Aids?
Costco can be a starting point if you’re just beginning to explore hearing aids. However, there are key differences to consider.

Most Costco locations are staffed by hearing aid specialists, not licensed audiologists . While they can provide basic services, they may not be trained to diagnose or treat more complex hearing conditions like tinnitus, sudden hearing loss, or balance-related ear issues.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, our audiologists are trained healthcare professionals with advanced degrees and years of experience. We’re here to provide comprehensive, compassionate care, not just a transaction.
Costco vs. Roberts Hearing Clinic: A Quick Comparison
Costco Offers:
Basic hearing screenings
Standard fittings
Limited follow-up care
Some tech features and demos
Roberts Hearing Clinic Offers:
Comprehensive hearing evaluations
Custom hearing aid fittings and real-ear measurements
Tinnitus evaluation and support
Follow-up visits, fine-tuning, and in-clinic cleanings
Hearing aid accessories, batteries, and repairs
Support from licensed audiologists
Costco May Offer Lower Prices, But What’s Missing?
Price:

Costco may offer a lower sticker price, but that doesn’t always include the level of care and customization your hearing health deserves. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, value means personal attention, quality technology, and long-term support.
Warranty:
Costco warranties can vary. We help you understand your warranty, handle repairs quickly, and offer fast, local service when you need it.
Batteries & Accessories:
We offer both rechargeable and disposable battery options, along with accessories like TV streamers, smartphone apps, and remote microphones with expert setup and ongoing support.
Does Costco Have Audiologists?
Most Costco locations do not employ audiologists. Their hearing centers are typically staffed by hearing aid specialists.
Hearing Aids in Alexandria, LA
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, our team includes licensed audiologists who are trained to identify, treat, and manage hearing conditions, ensuring you receive the highest level of care.
We offer a wide selection of hearing aids in Alexandria, LA to ensure that you get access to the best hearing solutions.
Contact us today to schedule an appointment!

Custom Hearing Protection
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides custom hearing protection in Alexandria, LA.

Protecting your hearing is essential-whether you’re at work, enjoying music, hunting, swimming, or trying to get a good night’s rest. At Roberts Hearing Clinic. our experienced Alexandria, LA audiologists provide custom hearing protection designed for comfort, safety, and long-term ear health.

Whether you’re a musician, hunter, industrial worker, or light sleeper, we offer both ready-made and custom-fit options , including earplugs, earmuffs, and advanced SoundGear digital protection . Our team will help you choose the best solution for your lifestyle and hearing needs.
Types of Hearing Protection
Ready-Made Hearing Protection
Pre-molded and easy to use, ready-made hearing protection is affordable and convenient, though it may not offer the same comfort or fit as custom options.
Earplugs – Inserted into the ear canal. Pros: Inexpensive and portable. Cons: May offer less comfort and a less secure fit.
Semi-Insert Earplugs – Connected by a band, resting at the ear canal entrance. Pros: Reusable and easy to wear. Cons: Less effective noise reduction.
Earmuffs – Cover the entire ear to block out external noise.
Pros: Strong protection. Cons: Bulkier and may become uncomfortable over time.
Custom Hearing Protection
Created from impressions of your ears, custom hearing protection provides the best fit, comfort, and sound blocking.
Custom Earplugs – Excellent for musicians, workers, or daily noise protection. Pros: Comfortable and long-lasting. Cons: Requires custom fitting.
Impulse Filter Earplugs – Ideal for hunters. These block loud gunshots while allowing softer sounds. Pros: Smart, responsive protection. Cons: Not for continuous noise.
Sleep Plugs – Soft and flexible for comfortable sleep. Pros: Designed for side sleepers. Cons: May block out important sounds like alarms.
In-Ear Monitors – Used by musicians and performers for high-quality sound. Pros: Exceptional sound clarity. Cons: Higher cost than standard earplugs.
SoundGear Digital Protection – Advanced hearing protection with digital sound filtering and clarity. Pros: Great for shooting and loud environments. Cons: Premium price.
Hearing Protection for Every Activity
At Roberts Hearing Clinic , our Alexandria, LA audiologists offer custom hearing protection tailored to your lifestyle:
Hunting – Impulse filter earplugs and SoundGear devices protect against gunfire while preserving natural sound awareness.
Music – Musicians’ earplugs and in-ear monitors reduce sound levels without distorting quality.
Swimming – Custom swim plugs help keep water out and prevent swimmer’s ear.
Sleeping – Sleep plugs reduce snoring and outside noise for better rest.
Work & Industry – Custom plugs and earmuffs protect workers in construction, manufacturing, and other loud environments.
Surfing & Water Sports – Surf plugs guard against wind and cold water exposure, helping prevent surfer’s ear.
Types of Custom Ear Molds
We offer a variety of materials for custom ear molds to ensure a perfect fit and comfort:
Vinyl – Soft and flexible, ideal for children or sensitive ears. Pros: Hypoallergenic and comfortable. Cons: Less durable over time.
Silicone – Durable, water-resistant, and flexible. Pros: Great for active users. Cons: Less adjustable after creation.
Acrylic – Hard, lightweight, and easy to clean. Pros: Durable and easy to insert. Cons: May not be ideal for sensitive ears.
Custom molds can be used for hearing aids, swimming, sleeping, or sound protection.
How Are Custom Ear Molds Made?

Our audiologists take a quick, painless impression of your ear canal. That impression is sent to a specialized lab where your ear mold is crafted from your chosen material. The result is a snug, secure fit tailored just for you. Custom ear molds offer a better seal, greater comfort, and improved noise reduction compared to generic options.
How Long Do Custom Earplugs Last?

With proper care, custom earplugs can last 3 to 5 years. Their durability depends on material type and usage. Regular cleaning and occasional fit checks—especially for children or those with changes in ear shape—help maintain performance.
Custom Hearing Protection in Alexandria, LA

At Roberts Hearing Clinic , we’re committed to helping you protect your hearing for the long term. Whether you need protection for work, music, hunting, swimming, or sleeping, our expert Alexandria, LA audiologists offer personalized solutions to keep your ears safe and comfortable.
Schedule your custom fitting appointment today and take the first step toward lasting hearing health.

children.text: Home » Diagnostic Services in Alexandria, LA
Diagnostic Services in Alexandria, LA
Roberts Hearing Clinic has audiologists providing diagnostic services in Alexandria, LA.

Diagnostic hearing tests help check how well you hear and find out if there are any problems with your ears. These tests help your audiologist understand the type, level, and cause of your hearing loss. With this information, we can recommend the best treatment-like hearing aids, medical care, or other hearing solutions.
We offer diagnostic services for the following hearing conditions.
Tinnitus

Tinnitus is a ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound in your ears that doesn’t come from anything around you. If you hear these sounds often, a tinnitus evaluation can help find out what’s causing it and how to treat it.

During your visit, your audiologist will ask about your symptoms, test your hearing, and use special tools to see how tinnitus affects your hearing and daily life. Treatment may include sound therapy, hearing aids, or relaxation exercises.
If tinnitus is bothering you, schedule a tinnitus evaluation today. We’re here to help you feel better.
Hearing Loss
Hearing loss means it’s harder for you to hear sounds clearly. It can be mild or very strong, and it can happen in one or both ears. You may notice:
Trouble understanding people, especially in noisy places
Asking others to repeat themselves
Turning up the volume on the TV or phone
Ringing or buzzing in the ears (tinnitus)
A hearing evaluation with an audiologist is the best way to check your hearing. It includes:
Talking about your medical history
Looking in your ears to check for wax or infections
Hearing tests to measure how well you hear sounds and speech
Sensorineural Hearing Loss (SNHL)
Sensorineural hearing loss happens when the inner ear or hearing nerve is damaged. This kind of hearing loss is permanent and can make it hard to understand sounds clearly.
Signs of SNHL may include:
Muffled or unclear speech
Trouble following conversations in noisy places
Difficulty hearing high-pitched sounds (like birds or alarms)
Ringing in the ears (tinnitus)
An audiologist can test for SNHL using:
Hearing tests to check how well you hear tones and speech
Speech tests to measure how clearly you hear words
Tympanometry to check how your middle ear is working
Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss (SSNHL)
Sudden sensorineural hearing loss, or sudden deafness, is a fast and unexpected loss of hearing in one ear. It usually happens over a few hours or days and is a medical emergency.
Common symptoms:
Sudden hearing loss in one ear
A full or blocked feeling in the ear
Dizziness or trouble with balance
Ringing in the ear (tinnitus)
Our audiologist will perform tests like:
A hearing test (audiogram) to measure your hearing
Tympanometry to check your middle ear function
You may also be referred to a doctor for more testing or medical treatment, like an MRI.
Diagnostic Services in Alexandria, LA
Your hearing health is an important part of your overall well-being.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic , we offer complete diagnostic services to help you hear your best. Whether you’ve noticed changes in your hearing or just want a check-up, we’re here to help.
Call us today to schedule your hearing test in Alexandria, LA!

Hearing Aid Alternatives: Assistive Listening Devices

Even the most advanced hearing aids can sometimes use a little support. Noisy restaurants, large group settings, or watching TV from across the room can still be challenging. That’s where assistive listening devices (ALDs) come in.

These helpful tools are designed to give your hearing an extra boost in specific situations. Whether you’re watching your favorite show, chatting on the phone, or attending a church service, ALDs can make sounds clearer and easier to understand—so you don’t miss a moment.
What’s the difference between hearing aids and assistive listening devices?

Hearing aids are custom-fit and designed to help with a wide range of everyday listening needs. But in certain environments-like classrooms, theaters, or crowded events-you may still struggle to hear clearly. That’s when assistive listening devices can really shine.

ALDs are task-specific tools that enhance sound in tough environments. They can be used on their own for people with mild hearing loss or together with hearing aids for added clarity. Best of all, they don’t require a hearing test or custom fitting and are often more affordable and easy to use.
Types of Assistive Listening Devices We Offer
Audio Induction or Hearing Loop Systems
A system that sends sound directly to hearing aids or cochlear implants equipped with a telecoil (T-coil) using electromagnetic fields.
Benefits:
Clear sound with less background noise
Perfect for public spaces like churches, theaters, and auditoriums
Works wirelessly with T-coil-equipped devices
Infrared Systems
Uses invisible light waves to transmit sound to a personal receiver worn with headphones or a neck loop.
Great for private conversations and TV listening
Common in courtrooms and home setups
No interference from other signals
FM Systems
Transmits sound via radio waves from a microphone worn by the speaker to a receiver used by the listener.
Excellent for classrooms and group discussions
Cuts through background noise and distance
Pairs easily with most hearing aids and cochlear implants
Personal Amplified Systems
Handheld or pocket-sized devices with headphones or earbuds that amplify nearby sound.
Easy to use and budget-friendly
Great for one-on-one chats or TV watching
No hearing test or fitting required
TV Listening Systems
Devices that send TV audio directly to wireless headphones or compatible receivers.
Clear sound without disturbing others
Crisp, enhanced dialogue
Multiple connection options like Bluetooth, infrared, or RF
Alerting Devices
These tools use lights, vibrations, or loud sounds to alert you to things like alarms, doorbells, or phone calls.
Boosts awareness and safety at home
Helpful for those with severe hearing loss
Can connect with smartphones and smart home systems
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the most commonly used assistive listening device?

FM systems are one of the most popular types, especially in schools and group settings. The speaker wears a microphone, and the listener hears them clearly through a personal receiver—perfect for cutting through noise and distance.
Why are assistive listening devices necessary?

Even with great hearing aids, certain environments can be tricky—like large rooms or noisy crowds. ALDs help by boosting sound exactly where you need it, improving communication and confidence in everyday life.
Can assistive listening devices replace hearing aids?

ALDs can be a great solution for people with mild hearing loss or for use in specific situations, but they don’t fully replace hearing aids for those with moderate to severe hearing loss. Most people benefit from using ALDs alongside their hearing aids for the best results.

children.text: Home » Hearing Aid Batteries
Hearing Aid Batteries
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides hearing aid batteries in Alexandria, LA to ensure that your hearing devices are always functioning at their best.

Hearing aid batteries power your hearing aids, making them work properly. Without the right battery, your hearing aids won’t help you hear well. Batteries affect how long your hearing aids last each day and how well they perform. Choosing the right type of battery is important for convenience and cost.
Two Types of Hearing Aid Batteries
Hearing aids use two main types of batteries: rechargeable batteries and standard disposable batteries . Each type has its own benefits.
Rechargeable Batteries

Rechargeable batteries are built into the hearing aid and do not need to be replaced often. You simply place your hearing aids in a charging case or dock overnight. By morning, they are fully charged and ready to use.
Benefits of rechargeable batteries:
No need to buy new batteries often
Easy to charge overnight
Better for the environment since they don’t create waste
Ideal for people who have trouble handling small batteries
However, rechargeable hearing aids must be charged daily. If you forget to charge them, they won’t work until recharged.
Standard Disposable Batteries

Disposable batteries are small, round batteries that you replace when they run out. These are also called zinc-air batteries. They are activated when you remove a small sticker from the battery, allowing air to enter.
Benefits of disposable batteries:
Can be replaced quickly when they run out
Useful if you don’t have a power source nearby to recharge
Last different lengths of time, depending on the battery size and hearing aid type
Disposable batteries can be helpful for people who travel often or do not have access to a charger. However, they need to be replaced regularly, which means ongoing costs.
Sizes of Disposable Hearing Aid Batteries
Disposable hearing aid batteries come in different sizes. Each size fits specific hearing aids.
Size 10 – Smallest battery, used in very small hearing aids. Lasts about 3-5 days.
Size 312 – A little bigger, common in behind-the-ear (BTE) and in-the-ear (ITE) hearing aids. Lasts about 5-7 days.
Size 13 – Larger than 312, used in powerful hearing aids. Lasts about 6-14 days.
Size 675 – Largest battery, used in very strong hearing aids. Lasts about 9-20 days.
Color-Coding for Disposable Hearing Aid Batteries
To make it easy to find the right size, battery packages use color codes:
Size 10 – Yellow
Size 312 – Brown
Size 13 – Orange
Size 675 – Blue
Battery Life of Hearing Aid Batteries
How long a hearing aid battery lasts depends on the battery size, the type of hearing aid, and how often you use it. On average:
Small batteries last 3-7 days
Larger batteries last 6-20 days
Rechargeable batteries last a full day but need daily charging
Using Bluetooth and other advanced hearing aid features can drain batteries faster.
How to Extend the Life of a Hearing Aid Battery
Taking care of your hearing aid batteries can help them last longer. Here are some tips:
Proper Storage and Handling:
Keep batteries in a cool, dry place.
Do not store them in the refrigerator.
Keep them away from metal objects, like keys and coins, to avoid short-circuiting.
Activating Zinc-Air Batteries:
Remove the sticker only when you are ready to use the battery .
Let the battery sit for 1-2 minutes before placing it in the hearing aid. This allows air to activate the battery fully.
Extending the Life of Rechargeable Batteries:
Charge hearing aids every night.
Do not overcharge them-use the charger designed for your hearing aid.
If storing hearing aids for a long time, turn them off to save battery life.
When to Replace Batteries:
If sounds become weak or unclear
If your hearing aid does not turn on
If you hear beeping sounds from the hearing aid (a low battery warning)

Need new hearing aid batteries?

At Roberts Hearing Clinic , we offer a wide range of hearing aid batteries. Whether you need rechargeable batteries or standard disposable ones, we can help you find the right fit for your hearing aids. Our audiologists are here to assist you in choosing the best option for your needs.
Visit or contact us to find the right batteries for your hearing aids!

Hearing Aid Fittings in Alexandria, LA
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides expert hearing aid fittings in Alexandria, LA.

A hearing aid fitting is when a hearing specialist adjusts your hearing aids to match your specific needs. This process ensures that your hearing aids provide clear, comfortable sound. Hearing aids do more than just make sounds louder-they need to be tuned to match your unique hearing loss for the best experience.
Why is a Professional Hearing Aid Fitting Important?

A professional fitting helps you get the best results from your hearing aids. Audiologists have the training and tools to adjust your hearing aids so that speech sounds clear and background noise is properly managed. A well-fitted hearing aid helps make sounds more natural and comfortable to hear.
Why Should an Audiologist Fit Your Hearing Aids?

Audiologists specialize in hearing and know how to properly fit and adjust hearing aids. If hearing aids are not fitted correctly, they can be uncomfortable or make sounds too loud or too soft. Seeing an audiologist ensures your hearing aids are set up correctly for your specific hearing needs.
What Happens During a Hearing Aid Fitting?
Step-by-Step Process of a Hearing Aid Fitting
Reviewing Your Hearing Test Results – The audiologist will explain your hearing loss and how hearing aids can help.
Choosing the Right Hearing Aid – Your audiologist will help you pick the best hearing aid for your lifestyle and needs.
Programming the Hearing Aids – Using special software, the audiologist adjusts the hearing aids to match your hearing levels.
Real Ear Measurement – A small microphone is placed in your ear to test how well your hearing aids work.
Learning How to Use Your Hearing Aids – The audiologist will show you how to put them in, take them out, and take care of them.
Scheduling Follow-up Appointments – Hearing aids often need fine-tuning, so follow-up visits are important.
What to Expect
Adjusting to Hearing Aids

When you first wear hearing aids, your brain needs time to adjust to new sounds. You may hear everyday noises more clearly, like the ticking of a clock or the sound of your footsteps. Over time, these sounds will start to feel normal again.
The Adjustment Period
Most people need a few weeks to get used to hearing aids. Here are some tips to help:
Start by wearing them for a few hours each day.
Increase wear time as you get more comfortable.
Practice listening in quiet places before using them in noisy settings.
Be patient-your brain needs time to adapt.
Follow-up Appointments

It’s important to return for follow-up visits so your audiologist can fine-tune your hearing aids. If sounds are too loud, too soft, or feel uncomfortable, adjustments can be made. These appointments help ensure your hearing aids work at their best.
Hearing Aid Fitting FAQs
Are hearing aid fittings covered by insurance?

Insurance coverage for hearing aid fittings depends on your provider. Medicare does not usually cover hearing aids, but some private insurance plans and Veterans Affairs benefits may offer coverage. Check with your provider to see what is included.
How can I make my hearing aid fit better?

If your hearing aid feels uncomfortable, your audiologist can adjust it. Different ear tips or custom molds can help improve the fit. Never try to force a hearing aid into your ear, as this can cause discomfort or poor sound quality.
How long does it take for a hearing aid to be fitted?
The first fitting usually takes about an hour. However, it may take a few weeks of adjustments to get the best fit and sound quality. Follow-up visits help make sure everything is working properly.

Hearing Aids & Products
Roberts Hearing Clinic has audiologists providing quality hearing aids and products in Alexandria, LA.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we proudly offer and service many of today’s most trusted hearing aid brands . Whether you’re already using hearing aids or exploring your options for the first time, our experienced team is here to help. We provide hearing aid fittings, programming, cleanings, repairs, and adjustments to keep your devices working their best.
We work with a wide range of reliable brands to ensure you get the best hearing technology to match your needs and lifestyle.
Hearing Aid Brands We Work With
Phonak Hearing Aids

Phonak is one of the most well-known hearing aid brands in the world, with more than 75 years of experience. Phonak hearing aids are designed with advanced features to help make conversations easier-especially in noisy places. Popular models like Phonak Lumity enhance speech understanding, while Phonak Naída is a strong solution for individuals with more severe hearing loss. Many Phonak devices offer Bluetooth streaming , rechargeable batteries , and water-resistant designs , making them practical for everyday use.
Oticon Hearing Aids

Oticon has been improving hearing health since 1904. Their hearing aids use BrainHearing™ technology , which supports the way your brain naturally processes sound. This helps reduce listening effort and improve clarity in noisy environments. Models like Oticon Real and Oticon More are designed to make speech easier to understand. Many Oticon hearing aids also include tinnitus relief features and wireless connectivity for added convenience.
Widex Hearing Aids

Widex hearing aids are known for their clear, natural sound . Since 1956, Widex has been delivering high-quality technology that reduces sound delays and enhances clarity. Models like Widex Moment and SmartRIC help make speech and background sounds feel more lifelike. Widex is also a top choice for individuals with tinnitus , offering built-in sound therapy programs , rechargeable options , and smartphone compatibility .
ReSound Hearing Aids

With over 75 years of innovation, ReSound hearing aids are known for their natural sound quality and excellent Bluetooth performance . Models like ReSound Omnia and ReSound ONE offer personalized hearing experiences by focusing on speech clarity and sound direction. ReSound also offers rechargeable options and tools for tinnitus management , making it a versatile choice for many users.
Starkey Hearing Aids

Starkey is a U.S.-based company that combines hearing technology with health and wellness features . Hearing aids like Starkey Genesis AI and Evolv AI offer benefits like fall detection , activity tracking , and tinnitus support . Starkey devices also allow for hands-free phone calls , rechargeable power , and easy smartphone connectivity.
Signia Hearing Aids

Signia hearing aids offer cutting-edge technology in sleek, stylish designs. Popular models like Signia Pure Charge&Go and Silk X provide Bluetooth streaming , speech clarity in noise , and rechargeable batteries . Signia also offers nearly invisible models that sit discreetly inside the ear. Some Signia hearing aids feature own-voice processing for a more natural sound experience.
Unitron Hearing Aids

Unitron hearing aids are designed for comfort and ease of use. Their technology automatically adjusts to different environments to help you hear more clearly throughout the day. A popular model like Unitron Blu includes Bluetooth streaming , rechargeable batteries , and a sleek, modern design . Unitron’s user-friendly app makes it simple to fine-tune your hearing experience and explore upgrade options.
Rexton Hearing Aids

Rexton has been developing reliable, user-friendly hearing aids for over 60 years. Known for their durability and high performance , Rexton hearing aids are great for everyday use. Popular models like Rexton BiCore and M-Core offer clear speech enhancement , Bluetooth connectivity , and rechargeable options . Many devices are water-resistant and designed for active lifestyles. Rexton’s smartphone app allows users to easily adjust settings and receive remote support when needed.
CaptionCall

CaptionCall is a free phone service for individuals with hearing loss who need help following conversations. The phone displays real-time captions on a screen while someone speaks, making it easier to understand what’s being said. You’ll need a hearing professional’s certification to qualify for the service.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the most advanced hearing aid?

Today’s top hearing aids offer speech clarity , Bluetooth connectivity , rechargeable batteries , and noise-reduction features . Each brand offers different strengths, so the “best” hearing aid depends on your hearing needs and lifestyle. Our team at Roberts Hearing Clinic can guide you to the right fit through a professional evaluation.
Which brand is best for tinnitus?

Many hearing aids offer features to help manage tinnitus. Brands like Widex , Oticon , and Starkey include sound therapy programs that ease ringing in the ears. An audiologist can help you choose the most effective hearing aid and treatment plan for your tinnitus needs.
Which hearing aid is best for severe hearing loss?

Hearing aids from Phonak , Oticon , and Starkey offer powerful solutions for severe to profound hearing loss. These devices provide high amplification, advanced speech processing, and custom settings. The right choice depends on your hearing test results and daily lifestyle.
Custom Hearing Protection

Custom earplugs are made just for your ears, offering better comfort and protection than store-bought versions. They’re perfect for work in loud environments, concerts, shooting sports, motorsports, or even swimming. Our hearing care professionals take a quick ear impression and provide a perfect fit that blocks harmful sounds without cutting you off from the world around you.
Custom Ear Molds

Custom ear molds are shaped to fit your ears precisely and are often used with hearing aids, in-ear monitors , hearing protection , or swim plugs . They improve sound quality, reduce feedback, and keep your hearing aids secure. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we’ll create a custom mold that fits comfortably and works with your specific needs.
Custom Ear Molds for Musicians

Musicians need both hearing protection and sound clarity . That’s why we offer custom solutions like musician earplugs and in-ear monitors . These custom molds help protect your ears from loud sounds while maintaining the high-quality audio musicians need during performances and practice sessions.
Frequently Asked Questions About Custom Ear Protection
Is it safe to sleep with earplugs?
Yes, sleeping with earplugs is safe—just make sure they are clean and fit properly to avoid irritation or ear infections.
How long do custom ear molds last?
Custom ear molds typically last 2 to 5 years , depending on how often you use them and how well you care for them.
Why are ear molds important for hearing aids?
Ear molds help improve fit, comfort, and sound quality . They also reduce whistling sounds (feedback) and help keep the hearing aid secure throughout the day.
Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs)

Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs) help improve hearing in specific situations-like watching TV, talking on the phone, or being in a group setting . ALDs can be used with or without hearing aids. Common types include:
TV Streamers
FM Systems
Personal Amplifiers
Hearing Loop Systems
Bluetooth Microphones
ALDs are great tools to improve your ability to hear speech clearly and stay involved in everyday conversations. Our team at Roberts Hearing Clinic can help you find the right device for your needs.
FAQs – Assistive Listening Devices
What’s the most commonly used ALD?
TV streamers and personal amplifiers are among the most popular. They help users hear more clearly in noisy or distant situations.
Can I use my iPhone as a listening device?
Yes! Apple’s Live Listen feature lets your iPhone act as a microphone and sends the sound directly to your hearing aids or headphones.
Where are ALDs required by law?
Public places like theaters, churches, classrooms, and government buildings are required to provide ALDs to help individuals with hearing loss better access sound.

Widex Hearing Aids
ReSound Hearing Aids
Starkey Hearing Aids
Signia Hearing Aids
Unitron Hearing Aids
Rexton Hearing Aids

Custom Ear Molds for Musicians

Hearing Aid Alternatives: Assistive Listening Devices

Even the most advanced hearing aids can sometimes use a little support. Noisy restaurants, large group settings, or watching TV from across the room can still be challenging. That’s where assistive listening devices (ALDs) come in.

These helpful tools are designed to give your hearing an extra boost in specific situations. Whether you’re watching your favorite show, chatting on the phone, or attending a church service, ALDs can make sounds clearer and easier to understand—so you don’t miss a moment.
What’s the difference between hearing aids and assistive listening devices?

Hearing aids are custom-fit and designed to help with a wide range of everyday listening needs. But in certain environments-like classrooms, theaters, or crowded events-you may still struggle to hear clearly. That’s when assistive listening devices can really shine.

ALDs are task-specific tools that enhance sound in tough environments. They can be used on their own for people with mild hearing loss or together with hearing aids for added clarity. Best of all, they don’t require a hearing test or custom fitting and are often more affordable and easy to use.
Types of Assistive Listening Devices We Offer
Audio Induction or Hearing Loop Systems
A system that sends sound directly to hearing aids or cochlear implants equipped with a telecoil (T-coil) using electromagnetic fields.
Benefits:
Clear sound with less background noise
Perfect for public spaces like churches, theaters, and auditoriums
Works wirelessly with T-coil-equipped devices
Infrared Systems
Uses invisible light waves to transmit sound to a personal receiver worn with headphones or a neck loop.
Great for private conversations and TV listening
Common in courtrooms and home setups
No interference from other signals
FM Systems
Transmits sound via radio waves from a microphone worn by the speaker to a receiver used by the listener.
Excellent for classrooms and group discussions
Cuts through background noise and distance
Pairs easily with most hearing aids and cochlear implants
Personal Amplified Systems
Handheld or pocket-sized devices with headphones or earbuds that amplify nearby sound.
Easy to use and budget-friendly
Great for one-on-one chats or TV watching
No hearing test or fitting required
TV Listening Systems
Devices that send TV audio directly to wireless headphones or compatible receivers.
Clear sound without disturbing others
Crisp, enhanced dialogue
Multiple connection options like Bluetooth, infrared, or RF
Alerting Devices
These tools use lights, vibrations, or loud sounds to alert you to things like alarms, doorbells, or phone calls.
Boosts awareness and safety at home
Helpful for those with severe hearing loss
Can connect with smartphones and smart home systems
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the most commonly used assistive listening device?

FM systems are one of the most popular types, especially in schools and group settings. The speaker wears a microphone, and the listener hears them clearly through a personal receiver—perfect for cutting through noise and distance.
Why are assistive listening devices necessary?

Even with great hearing aids, certain environments can be tricky—like large rooms or noisy crowds. ALDs help by boosting sound exactly where you need it, improving communication and confidence in everyday life.
Can assistive listening devices replace hearing aids?

ALDs can be a great solution for people with mild hearing loss or for use in specific situations, but they don’t fully replace hearing aids for those with moderate to severe hearing loss. Most people benefit from using ALDs alongside their hearing aids for the best results.

Starkey Hearing Aids
Roberts Hearing Clinic is an authorized provider of Starkey hearing aids in Alexandria, LA.

Starkey is known for creating advanced hearing aids that help people hear better in all kinds of situations. Starkey hearing aids are small, custom-fit hearing aids that are comfortable and reliable for various listening situations.
Starkey also uses artificial intelligence (AI) to improve sound quality and make listening easier. Their wide range of hearing aids fits different needs and lifestyles.
Current Starkey Hearing Aid Models
Starkey Omega AI

Starkey Omega AI is built with industry-leading technology that gives users powerful sound clarity and day-long comfort. Its advanced AI system constantly analyzes your surroundings to help you hear speech clearly, stay aware of important sounds, and move through different environments with ease.

If you struggle with hearing in noisy places, Omega AI’s Edge Mode+ provides on-demand help by sharpening speech instantly, even in challenging spaces like restaurants, shopping centers, or family gatherings.

These hearing aids are also designed for durability. With a 10x more durable waterproof coating, Omega AI can handle rain, sweat, and everyday wear without worry. Rechargeable options give all-day power, keeping you connected from morning to night.
Unique Features:
Edge Mode+: Boosts speech clarity during tough listening moments.
Waterproof & Everyday-Proof: Designed for active lifestyles and all-day comfort.
Auracast™ & LE Audio Ready: Allows streaming from TVs, smartphones, public announcement systems, and more.
Starkey App (Now Powered by Gen AI): Use TeleHear AI for instant, AI-based sound adjustments.
Starkey Signature Series

The Starkey Signature Series gives you amazing sound in hearing aids that are super tiny and almost invisible. They are custom-made to fit inside your ear, so no one can tell you’re wearing them. You’ll hear your friends, family, and the world around you clearly, without anyone knowing why. Whether you want rechargeable, adjustable, or the smallest size possible, there’s a signature style just for you.
Discreet: Nearly invisible and fits deep in your ear.
Natural Sound: Clear, lifelike sound so you can enjoy every moment.
Rechargeable: Up to 38 hours of power—no tiny batteries to change.
Waterproof: Designed to handle water up to 1 meter deep.
Custom Fit: Made just for your ears for all-day comfort and security.
Starkey Edge AI
Starkey Edge AI hearing aids use AI to improve sound clarity and reduce background noise. A powerful smart chip helps focus on speech so users can hear better in noisy places.

Edge AI adjusts automatically to different environments, making speech 30% clearer than older models. Whether you’re at a party, restaurant, or at home, these hearing aids help you understand conversations better.
Built to Last: Waterproof up to 1 meter and sweat-resistant.
Strong Bluetooth Connection: Works with smartphones and connects easily to TVs and public sound systems using Auracast™.
Health & Safety Features: Includes balance exercises and fall detection.
Easy App Control: The My Starkey app allows you to adjust settings, control volume, stream calls, and find lost hearing aids. Compatible with smartphones and Apple Watch.
Starkey Genesis AI RIC

The Starkey Genesis AI hearing aids use smart technology to help people hear soft sounds clearly, understand speech better, and reduce listening effort. The AI adapts to different situations, ensuring great sound wherever you go.

Genesis AI receiver-in-the-canal (RIC) hearing aids work for mild to severe hearing loss. They come in rechargeable or disposable battery options. The rechargeable battery lasts up to 51 hours on a full charge and can provide 3 hours of use with just a 7-minute charge.
Waterproof: Special coating protects against sweat, rain, and dirt.
Bluetooth Connectivity: The My Starkey app lets users adjust settings, stream calls, and locate lost hearing aids.
Remote Support: TeleHear allows remote adjustments via video chat.
Tinnitus Relief: Custom sound options help manage ringing in the ears.
Starkey Genesis AI ITE

Starkey’s in-the-ear (ITE) hearing aids are custom-made to fit comfortably. The Genesis AI ITE uses a smart processor that works like the human brain to provide clear and natural sound in different environments.

These hearing aids work for mild to severe hearing loss. They come in rechargeable and disposable battery options. The latest Genesis AI ITE model is the smallest wireless CIC hearing aid, offering a nearly invisible fit without reducing sound quality.
Waterproof: Special layers protect the hearing aid from water, sweat, and dust.
Bluetooth Connectivity: Connects to smartphones for easy control.
Remote Support: Adjustments can be made remotely through video chat.
Tinnitus Relief: Custom sound options help reduce ringing in the ears.
Starkey CROS

Starkey’s CROS hearing aids help people who have hearing loss in one ear. These devices pick up sound from the weaker ear and send it to the stronger ear, making it easier to hear conversations and sounds around you.
The CROS hearing aids work with the Genesis AI models and some older Starkey models.
Starkey Evolv AI BTE

Starkey’s Evolv AI behind-the-ear (BTE) hearing aids adjust automatically to the environment to improve hearing. They make 55 million automatic adjustments every hour and help reduce background noise, such as wind and machine sounds.
Evolv AI BTE hearing aids work for mild to severe hearing loss. They come with rechargeable or disposable battery options.
Bluetooth Connectivity: Works with the Thrive Hearing Control app for easy adjustments.
Remote Support: Adjustments can be made through video chat.
Tinnitus Relief: Custom sound programs help reduce ringing in the ears.
Starkey Evolv AI Power Plus BTE
The Starkey Evolv AI Power Plus BTE has the same features as the Evolv AI BTE but provides more power for people with severe to profound hearing loss.
These hearing aids use a size 13 disposable battery.
Bluetooth Connectivity: Connects with the Thrive Hearing Control app for easy settings.
Remote Support: Adjustments can be made remotely.
Tinnitus Relief: Custom sound settings to help reduce ringing in the ears.
Assistive Listening Devices & Technology by Starkey
Mini Remote Microphone
Remote Mic +
Remote Control 2.0
Table Microphone
TV Streamer
Older Starkey Hearing Aid Models Supported by Roberts Hearing Clinic
If you have an older Starkey hearing aid, we may still be able to service or repair it.
Starkey Picasso
Starkey Livio
Starkey Muse iQ
Starkey Halo iQ
Starkey Halo 2
Starkey Halo
Please contact us for more details.
Frequently Asked Questions About Starkey Hearing Aids
What are the tech levels of Starkey Genesis AI?
There are four technology levels: 24 (highest), 20, 16, and 12 (lowest). A CROS model is also available for people with severe hearing loss in one ear.
What app does Starkey Genesis AI use?
The My Starkey app connects with Genesis AI hearing aids. It lets users adjust settings, track their well-being, and find lost hearing aids.
How long do Starkey hearing aids last?

In-the-ear hearing aids usually last about five years, while behind-the-ear hearing aids last five to six years. How well you take care of them can affect their lifespan. Some people upgrade earlier to get the latest technology. An audiologist can help you decide when it’s time for a new hearing aid.

children.text: Home » Hearing Tests in Alexandria, LA
Hearing Tests in Alexandria, LA
Roberts Hearing Clinic provides comprehensive hearing tests in Alexandria, LA.

A hearing test helps determine how well you hear different sounds. At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we use advanced tests to identify hearing issues and find the best solutions. Our expert audiologists in Alexandria, LA are here to support your hearing health.
Why Would I Need a Hearing Test?
Hearing loss can develop slowly, making it hard to notice at first. Common signs include:
Struggling to hear in noisy places
Asking people to repeat themselves
Turning up the volume on the TV or phone
Ringing or buzzing in the ears
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we offer a variety of hearing tests, including:
Pure-tone audiometry – Measures how well you hear different tones.
Speech testing – Determines how well you understand speech.
Tympanometry – Evaluates the movement of the eardrum.
What Are the Types of Hearing Tests?
Pure-Tone Audiometry – Determines the softest sounds you can hear at different frequencies.
Speech Audiometry – Measures how well you understand words at various volume levels.
Tympanometry – Checks for middle ear problems, like fluid buildup or eardrum issues.
Three Main Types of Hearing Loss
Sensorineural Hearing Loss – Caused by damage to the inner ear or hearing nerve. Often permanent and treated with hearing aids or cochlear implants.
Conductive Hearing Loss – Occurs when sound can’t travel through the outer or middle ear. Often treatable with medication or surgery.
Mixed Hearing Loss – A combination of sensorineural and conductive hearing loss, requiring specialized treatment.
Hearing Test: What to Expect

During your test, you’ll wear headphones and listen to different tones. The audiologist will also check your ear health and ask about your hearing history. The test is painless and takes about 30 to 45 minutes.
Hearing Test Results

Once the test is complete, the audiologist will explain your results using an audiogram (a graph of your hearing ability). If hearing loss is found, we will discuss treatment options, such as hearing aids or medical referrals.
Hearing Test FAQs
Can I test my own hearing?
You can take an online hearing test, but it won’t be as accurate as a professional test with an audiologist. Roberts Hearing Clinic provides comprehensive hearing tests in Alexandria, LA.
Will I need to do anything to prepare for a hearing test?
No special preparation is needed, but try to avoid loud noise before your test.
Are there any risks to hearing tests?
No, hearing tests are safe and painless.
How reliable are online hearing tests?
Online tests can give you a rough idea of your hearing, but they are not as precise as a full audiological exam. Roberts Hearing Clinic provides comprehensive hearing tests in Alexandria, LA.
Can you do a hearing test on your phone?
Some apps provide basic hearing checks, but they can’t replace a professional hearing evaluation.
How often should I take a hearing test?
Adults with normal hearing should have a hearing test every 3 to 5 years . If you have hearing loss, wear hearing aids, or work in a noisy environment, you should get a hearing test once a year .
Hearing Tests in Alexandria, LA
Your hearing is an essential part of your quality of life. Our Audiology team at Roberts Hearing Clinic are experts in providing comprehensive hearing tests in Alexandria, LA.
Schedule your hearing test today and take the first step toward better hearing!

children.text: Home » Should You Trust Nano Hearing Aids? An Audiologist’s Take
Should You Trust Nano Hearing Aids? An Audiologist’s Take

Nano hearing aids are small devices you can buy online to help you hear better. They are made to make sounds louder and come in styles that fit inside or behind your ear. The company says you don’t need a hearing test or a visit to the doctor. You just order online and start using them.

That might sound easy, but hearing loss is different for every person. Some people might need more powerful hearing help or special settings. Nano hearing aids don’t check your hearing or fit your ears the right way. They are a “one-size-fits-all” option, and that doesn’t always work well.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, our audiologists in Alexandria, LA , check your hearing first, then help you find the best hearing aid for your needs. We believe hearing care should be personal, not something you guess at online.
Buying Hearing Aids Online: Pros and Cons
Pros
You can order from home
Usually less expensive
Quick shipping
Cons
No hearing test
May not match your hearing loss
Can be uncomfortable or too loud
Hard to return or get help
No in-person support

Some reviews say Nano hearing aids help a little in quiet rooms. Others say they whistle, stop working, or don’t fit right. Many customers are frustrated because they can’t return them easily or get help when they need it.
Hearing loss is personal. Buying hearing aids online may be cheap, but it’s not always the best or safest choice.
A Short History of Nano Hearing Aids

Nano Hearing Aids is a company that started selling hearing devices online a few years ago. They advertise their products as affordable and simple to use. The ads often say their hearing aids are “FDA registered” and almost invisible.

They became popular because of their low prices and easy ordering. But over time, many people started complaining about the quality. Customers reported problems with the sound, fit, battery life, and customer service. The Better Business Bureau (BBB) has also received many complaints about refunds and returns.
Nano products are real, but they are not custom-made for your ears. And without an audiologist involved, there’s no way to know if they are right for your hearing loss.
Are Nano Hearing Aids Good for Severe Hearing Loss?
Nano hearing aids might help people with very mild hearing loss in quiet places. But they are not a good option for severe hearing loss .
Severe hearing loss often needs more powerful hearing aids with special features, like:
Noise reduction
Directional microphones
Custom volume settings
Bluetooth connection
Tinnitus relief
Nano hearing aids don’t offer most of these features. They simply make sounds louder-and sometimes that includes background noise you don’t want to hear.
Another problem is fit. Nano hearing aids are not custom-fitted. If they don’t fit your ears just right, they might be uncomfortable, fall out, or not work well.

At Roberts Hearing Clinic , we take the time to test your hearing and recommend hearing aids made for your ears and your level of hearing loss. We make sure the fit is comfortable, the sound is clear, and the device is helping you in the way it should.
Nano Hearing Aid Prices
Nano hearing aids usually cost between $297 and $597 per pair . That’s cheaper than many hearing aids from a clinic, but the lower price often means fewer features, no testing, and no in-person help.
Are Nano Hearing Aids a Scam?
Nano hearing aids are not fake-but they’re not right for everyone either. Many people have reported problems with how they work, how they fit, or how hard it is to get a refund.
If you don’t know what kind of hearing loss you have, you’re taking a big risk by buying hearing aids without a test.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic , we offer something better:
A full hearing test
Custom-fitted hearing aids
Follow-up visits and care
Help with cleaning and repairs
Friendly, local audiologists who care about your hearing
We carry a wide range of hearing aids-from simple, affordable models to advanced devices with smart features. No matter your budget or hearing needs, we’ll help you find the best fit.
Instead of guessing with an online product, come see us first . We’ll make sure you get the care, comfort, and clarity you deserve.
What Our Audiologists Say About Nano Hearing Aids
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we believe good hearing starts with good care. Nano hearing aids may seem like a quick fix, but they skip the most important step: seeing an audiologist.
If your hearing aid isn’t matched to your ears or your hearing needs, it might not help at all. In some cases, it can even make hearing worse.
That’s why we recommend getting a hearing test first. With the right diagnosis and a hearing aid fitted just for you, you’ll hear better and feel better every day.
Visit our audiologists in Alexandria, LA today, and let us help you take the first step toward better hearing with expert care and support.

children.text: Home » Oticon Hearing Aids
Oticon Hearing Aids
Roberts Hearing Clinic is an authorized provider of Oticon hearing aids in Alexandria, LA.

Oticon is a global leader in hearing technology, dedicated to helping people hear and communicate with confidence. With a strong focus on research and innovation, Oticon creates hearing aids that provide clear, natural sound and an improved listening experience.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic , we share Oticon’s commitment to offering the best hearing solutions. Our goal is to help you hear better in every situation, whether at home, work, or social gatherings.
Current Phonak Hearing Aid Models
Oticon Zeal

Oticon Zeal is the first hearing aid designed to do it all while staying completely unseen. Built for people who want powerful technology in an ultra-discreet design, Zeal delivers exceptional sound clarity, all-day comfort, and seamless connectivity in one tiny device no one will notice.

Zeal transforms the idea of what a hearing aid should be. Its small, nearly invisible design sits comfortably in your ear, giving you the confidence to live fully without drawing attention to your device. Powered by Oticon’s advanced BrainHearing™ technology, Zeal supports the brain’s natural way of processing sound. Enjoy clear, balanced, and comfortable hearing, even in noisy places.
Unique Features:

Made to Connect : Stream calls, meetings, music, and more directly from your phone, Apple Watch, TV, computer, or tablet. Zeal brings your digital world to life with smooth, high-quality wireless audio.
Reliable Rechargeability: No disposable batteries. With fast, dependable charging, you get all-day power that keeps up with your lifestyle.
Same-Day Fitting: Zeal is designed for convenience, offering the option for same-day fitting so you can begin hearing better right away.
Oticon Jet PX

Oticon Jet PX is a smart hearing aid that uses advanced technology (called Deep Neural Network or DNN) to help you hear clearly. With features like Wind Noise Management and Speech Guard, it helps block out sounds that get in the way of talking to others.

If you have ringing in your ears (tinnitus), Jet PX has built-in sounds to help you feel better. You can also connect it to your phone to listen to music, take calls, or change settings using the Oticon app. It comes in different colors and styles, and you can even get a rechargeable version.
AI-powered OpenSound Navigator with DNN : Improves hearing with clear, natural sound.
Tinnitus SoundSupport: Ideal for users with tinnitus as it gives access to customizable relief sounds.
SuperShield : Quickly adapts and prevents feedback before it occurs.
Oticon Own SI

Oticon Own SI hearing aids are tiny, comfortable devices that fit inside your ears and help you hear clearly again. It comes with two small styles to choose from – one that’s nearly invisible and another with easy-to-use buttons.
These custom-made hearing aids are built with special BrainHearing technology to support how your brain naturally understands sound, helping you feel more connected to the people around you.
Discreet and sophisticated: Super small styles (IIC and CIC) that fit fully in your ear
BrainHearing™ technology : Helps your brain make sense of sound.
Custom-fit: Built for all-day comfort, even with glasses or masks.
Strong and durable: Water- and dust-resistant to last through busy days.
Oticon Intent

The Oticon Intent hearing aid adapts to your needs in real-time, even in noisy places. It features 4D Sensor Technology , which tracks movement, speech, and surrounding sounds to deliver the best hearing experience.
With Deep Neural Network (DNN) technology , Oticon Intent mimics the brain’s natural way of processing sound, making conversations clearer and reducing listening effort.
Key Features:
Bluetooth® LE Audio – Connects to multiple devices for direct streaming.

Zeal transforms the idea of what a hearing aid should be. Phonak Hearing Aids
Roberts Hearing Clinic is an authorized provider of Phonak hearing aids in Alexandria, LA.
At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we believe that good hearing improves overall well-being. Phonak shares this belief with their motto, “Well-Hearing is Well-Being.”
Hearing isn’t just about sound—it helps with thinking, emotions, and social connections. Phonak’s advanced hearing aids are designed to help people hear better, stay connected, and enjoy life.
Current Phonak Hearing Aid Models
Phonak Infinio Ultra Line

The Phonak Infinio Ultra Line represents the next evolution in hearing technology, delivering elevated clarity, efficiency, and adaptability through advanced AI processing. Released in October 2025, this flagship upgrade enhances the foundational Infinio platform with smarter sound recognition, better battery performance, and simplified maintenance.

For many existing Phonak users, these improvements can be activated through an in-clinic firmware update, allowing current Infinio or Infinio Sphere devices to perform at an entirely new level without requiring new hardware.
Infinio Ultra R
A flexible, ultra-adaptive model powered by AutoSense OS™ 7.0, designed to automatically adjust to a wide range of environments. Ideal for patients seeking seamless performance in everyday listening.
Infinio Ultra Sphere

Engineered for complex and noisy situations, this model features Spheric Speech Clarity 2.0 and the breakthrough DEEPSONIC™ AI chip, the world’s first dedicated processor for real-time speech separation. This allows clearer understanding of multiple speakers from any direction, even in the most challenging soundscapes.
Unique Features:
AutoSense OS™ 7.0 adapts with 24% greater precision and is trained on 18× more sound scenarios, resulting in smarter environmental transitions and more natural listening.
Spheric Speech Clarity 2.0 (Ultra Sphere only) enhances speech up to threefold in noisy settings by isolating voices and reducing background interference.
Listening effort is reduced by up to 35% , supporting long-term comfort and decreasing auditory fatigue.
Phonak Virto Infinio

Phonak Virto Infinio is a custom in-the-ear (ITE) hearing aid released in 2025, built for those who want powerful performance in a discreet design. Each device is custom-molded to match the shape of your ear, giving you a snug, comfortable fit that lasts all day.
Packed with advanced sound technology, Virto Infinio delivers clear, natural hearing in a small, almost invisible shell, perfect for anyone who wants great sound without drawing attention.
Custom-Made Fit: Each device is individually molded to the shape of your ear, ensuring a secure, comfortable fit that’s easy to wear all day.
AutoSense OS 6.0: Automatically adjusts settings based on your surroundings, providing seamless hearing whether you’re in quiet, noisy, or dynamic environments.
Durable & Water-Resistant: Rated IP68 for dust and moisture resistance, making it ideal for active lifestyles and daily wear.
Multiple Technology Levels: Available in four tiers (I90, I70, I50, I30) to meet a range of hearing needs and budgets.
Phonak Audéo Sphere

This high-tech hearing aid delivers clear sound and adjusts automatically to different environments. Whether you’re in a quiet setting, a noisy café, or listening to music, the Audéo Sphere adapts for the best experience.
Key Features:
Rechargeable Battery – A full day of power on a single charge.
Smart Sound Processing – Separates speech from background noise.
Bluetooth Connectivity – Connects to phones for calls, music, and volume control.
Phonak Audéo Infinio
The Audéo Infinio enhances speech clarity in noisy places while reducing listening effort. It adjusts sound levels automatically and connects seamlessly to smartphones.
CROS Compatibility – Helps those with hearing loss in one ear.
Roger Direct Ready – Improves hearing in loud environments and over distances.
Multiple Bluetooth Connections – Pairs with up to 8 devices and connects to 2 at the same time.
Phonak CROS Infinio
Designed for single-sided deafness, this device sends sound from the non-hearing side to the better-hearing ear, making conversations easier.
Hands-Free Calling & Streaming – Works over a longer distance.
Rechargeable Battery – Convenient and long-lasting.
Universal Bluetooth Connectivity – Pairs with most Bluetooth devices.
Phonak Audéo Fit
Perfect for active individuals, the Audéo Fit tracks health data like steps, activity levels, and heart rate using the myPhonak app.
Health Tracking – Monitors movement and well-being.
Tap Control – Easily answer calls, adjust volume, and change settings.
Universal Bluetooth Connectivity – Connects to smartphones, TVs, and other devices.
Phonak Audéo Lumity
The Audéo Lumity is designed to improve speech clarity in challenging listening environments. It uses AI-based technology to adapt to various settings, making conversations easier to follow.
Bluetooth Connectivity – Pairs with the myPhonak app and other Bluetooth devices.
Customizable Settings – Adjust preferences through the app.
Remote Support – Get virtual help from a hearing care provider.
Phonak Slim
The Phonak Slim has the same advanced technology as the Audéo Lumity but in a sleek, modern design that fits comfortably behind the ear-perfect for those who wear glasses.
Ergonomic Design – Stylish and comfortable fit.
Bluetooth & App Control – Easily adjust hearing settings.
Rechargeable Battery – All-day hearing support.
Phonak CROS Lumity
For single-sided hearing loss, the CROS Lumity helps users hear from all directions while reducing background noise.
Wireless Sound Transmission – Sends sound from the non-hearing ear to the hearing ear.
Bluetooth Connectivity – Connects with the myPhonak app and other Bluetooth devices.
Remote Assistance – Receive virtual support from a hearing professional.
Phonak Naída Lumity
Built for individuals with severe to profound hearing loss, the Naída Lumity scans the environment 700 times per second to ensure the best sound quality.
Bluetooth Connectivity – Pairs with phones and other smart devices.
Customizable Settings – Adjust preferences through the myPhonak app.
Multiple Power Options – Available in rechargeable and traditional battery models.
Phonak Sky Lumity
Designed for children, the Sky Lumity hearing aid helps kids hear better at school, home, and during play.
SmartSpeech™ Technology – Focuses on speech instead of background noise.
Kid-Friendly App – The myPhonak Junior app allows kids to control their hearing settings.
Tamper-Resistant Design – Safe for young users.
Phonak Virto Paradise
The Virto Paradise is a custom-fit hearing aid that sits discreetly inside the ear. It reduces background noise and enhances speech clarity.
Custom Fit – Molded to match the shape of your ear.
Bluetooth Connectivity – Works with smartphones and TVs.
Multiple Battery Options – Available in various sizes.
Phonak Assistive Devices
Phonak also offers accessories to improve hearing in specific situations:
Phonak Serenity Choice – Protects ears from loud noises while keeping speech clear.
Roger On – A microphone that enhances conversations in noisy environments.
Roger Select – A table microphone that helps in group conversations.

  • Multiple Bluetooth Connections – Pairs with up to 8 devices and connects to 2 at the same time.

Phonak CROS Infinio

Designed for single-sided deafness, this device sends sound from the non-hearing side to the better-hearing ear, making conversations easier.

Key Features:

  • Hands-Free Calling & Streaming – Works over a longer distance.
  • Rechargeable Battery – Convenient and long-lasting.
  • Universal Bluetooth Connectivity – Pairs with most Bluetooth devices.

Phonak Audéo Fit

Perfect for active individuals, the Audéo Fit tracks health data like steps, activity levels, and heart rate using the myPhonak app.

Key Features:

  • Health Tracking – Monitors movement and well-being.
  • Tap Control – Easily answer calls, adjust volume, and change settings.
  • Universal Bluetooth Connectivity – Connects to smartphones, TVs, and other devices.

Phonak Audéo Lumity

The Audéo Lumity is designed to improve speech clarity in challenging listening environments. It uses AI-based technology to adapt to various settings, making conversations easier to follow.

Key Features:

  • Bluetooth Connectivity – Pairs with the myPhonak app and other Bluetooth devices.
  • Customizable Settings – Adjust preferences through the app.
  • Remote Support – Get virtual help from a hearing care provider.

Phonak Slim

The Phonak Slim has the same advanced technology as the Audéo Lumity but in a sleek, modern design that fits comfortably behind the ear-perfect for those who wear glasses.

Key Features:

  • Ergonomic Design – Stylish and comfortable fit.
  • Bluetooth & App Control – Easily adjust hearing settings.
  • Rechargeable Battery – All-day hearing support.

Phonak CROS Lumity

For single-sided hearing loss, the CROS Lumity helps users hear from all directions while reducing background noise.

Key Features:

  • Wireless Sound Transmission – Sends sound from the non-hearing ear to the hearing ear.
  • Bluetooth Connectivity – Connects with the myPhonak app and other Bluetooth devices.
  • Remote Assistance – Receive virtual support from a hearing professional.

Phonak Naída Lumity

Built for individuals with severe to profound hearing loss, the Naída Lumity scans the environment 700 times per second to ensure the best sound quality.

Key Features:

  • Bluetooth Connectivity – Pairs with phones and other smart devices.
  • Customizable Settings – Adjust preferences through the myPhonak app.
  • Multiple Power Options – Available in rechargeable and traditional battery models.

Phonak Sky Lumity

Designed for children, the Sky Lumity hearing aid helps kids hear better at school, home, and during play.

Key Features:

  • SmartSpeech™ Technology – Focuses on speech instead of background noise.
  • Kid-Friendly App – The myPhonak Junior app allows kids to control their hearing settings.
  • Tamper-Resistant Design – Safe for young users.

Phonak Virto Paradise

The Virto Paradise is a custom-fit hearing aid that sits discreetly inside the ear. It reduces background noise and enhances speech clarity.

Key Features:

  • Custom Fit – Molded to match the shape of your ear.
  • Bluetooth Connectivity – Works with smartphones and TVs.
  • Multiple Battery Options – Available in various sizes.

Phonak Assistive Devices

Phonak also offers accessories to improve hearing in specific situations:

  • Phonak Serenity Choice – Protects ears from loud noises while keeping speech clear.
  • Roger On – A microphone that enhances conversations in noisy environments.
  • Roger Select – A table microphone that helps in group conversations.
  • TV Connector – Streams TV sound directly to your hearing aids.
  • PartnerMic – A clip-on microphone for one-on-one conversations.

Older Phonak Hearing Aids We Service

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we continue to repair and maintain older Phonak models, including:

  • Phonak Audéo Paradise
  • Phonak Naída Paradise
  • Phonak CROS Paradise
  • Phonak Naída Link Marvel
  • Phonak Sky Marvel
  • Phonak Audéo Marvel
  • Phonak Bolero B
  • Phonak Naída B
  • Phonak Virto B
  • Phonak Audéo B

 

Need repairs or support? Contact us today!

Frequently Asked Questions About Phonak Hearing Aids

What are the different levels of Phonak Lumity?

Phonak Lumity comes in four levels: L90, L70, L50, and L30. L90 has the most advanced features, while L30 offers basic features for everyday hearing.

What is Phonak Life?

Phonak Audéo Life™ Lumity is the first waterproof rechargeable hearing aid. It’s designed for people with active lifestyles who need extra protection from water and sweat.

How is Phonak Life different from Phonak Paradise?

Phonak Audéo Life is more water-resistant than Phonak Paradise. It has all the same great features but is better suited for people who exercise, swim, or spend time in wet environments.

Find the Right Phonak Hearing Aid for You

At Roberts Hearing Clinic, we help you choose the best Phonak hearing aid for your needs. We are an authorized provider of Phonak hearing aids in Alexandria, LA.

Roberts Hearing Clinic Privacy Policy
This Privacy Policy describes how your personal information is collected, used, and shared when you visit or make a purchase from / (the “Site”).
PERSONAL INFORMATION WE COLLECT

When you visit the Site, we automatically collect certain information about your device, including information about your web browser, IP address, time zone, and some of the cookies that are installed on your device. Additionally, as you browse the Site, we collect information about the individual web pages or products that you view, what websites or search terms referred you to the Site, and information about how you interact with the Site. We refer to this automatically collected information as “ Device Information .”
We collect Device Information using the following technologies:

“ Cookies ” are data files that are placed on your device or computer and often include an anonymous unique identifier. For more information about cookies, and how to disable cookies, visit http://www.allaboutcookies.org.
“ Log files ” track actions occurring on the Site, and collect data including your IP address, browser type, Internet service provider, referring/exit pages, and date/time stamps.
“ Web beacons ”, “ tags ”, and “ pixels ” are electronic files used to record information about how you browse the Site.

Additionally, when you make a purchase or attempt to make a purchase through the Site, we collect certain information from you, including your name, billing address, shipping address, payment information (including credit card numbers), email address, and phone number. We refer to this information as “ Order Information. ”
When we talk about “Personal Information” in this Privacy Policy, we are talking about both Device Information and Order Information.
HOW DO WE USE YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION?

We use the Order Information that we collect generally to fulfill any orders placed through the Site (including processing your payment information, arranging for shipping, and providing you with invoices and/or order confirmations). Additionally, we use this Order Information to:
communicate with you;
screen our orders for potential risk or fraud; and
provide you with information or advertising relating to our products or services (depending on the preferences you have shared with us)

We use the Device Information that we collect to help us screen for potential risk and fraud (in particular, your IP address), and more generally to improve and optimize our Site (for example, by generating analytics about how our customers browse and interact with the Site), and to assess the success of our marketing and advertising campaigns.
SHARING YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION
We may share your Personal Information with third parties as needed to help us use your Personal Information, as described above.

We also use Google Analytics to help us understand how our customers use the Site–you can read more about how Google uses your Personal Information here: https://www.google.com/intl/en/policies/privacy/. You can also opt out of Google Analytics here: https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout.

Finally, we may also share your Personal Information to comply with applicable laws and regulations, to respond to a subpoena, search warrant, or other lawful request for information we receive, or to otherwise protect our rights.
BEHAVIOURAL ADVERTISING

As described above, we may use your Personal Information to provide you with targeted advertisements or marketing communications we believe may be of interest to you. For more information about how targeted advertising works, you can visit the Network Advertising Initiative’s (“NAI”) educational page at http://www.networkadvertising.org/understanding-online-advertising/how-does-it-work.
You can opt out of and/or adjust targeted advertising on:
Facebook by going to https://www.facebook.com/settings/?tab=ads
Google by going to https://www.google.com/settings/ads/anonymous
Bing by going to https://advertise.bingads.microsoft.com/en-us/resources/policies/personalized-ads
Additionally, you can opt out of some of these services by visiting the Digital Advertising Alliance’s opt-out portal at: http://optout.aboutads.info/.
DO NOT TRACK
Please note that we do not alter our Site’s data collection and use practices when we see a Do Not Track signal from your browser.
DATA RETENTION
When you place an order through the Site, we will maintain your Order Information for our records unless and until you ask us to delete this information.
CHANGES
We may update this privacy policy from time to time in order to reflect, for example, changes to our practices or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons.
CONTACT US

For more information about our privacy practices, if you have questions, or if you would like to make a complaint, please contact us by e-mail at leads@onephg.com or by mail using the details provided below:
4007 Parliament Drive
Alexandria, LA 71303
